Sections 1224.14.1, 1224.14.3, 1224.4.10 and 1224.4.11 form a coherent requirement set governing hospital patient room dimensions, isolation, ceiling heights, and interior finishes.

hyperedges.label: Accessible Route Provisions Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 11B-206 (scoping) and 11B-402 through 11B-407 (Division 4 technical) together constitute the complete accessible route requirement framework: where required, what components are allowed, and how each component must be built.

hyperedges.label: Alteration Path of Travel Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 11B-202 and 11B-202.4 together with the valuation threshold and unreasonable hardship concepts govern the entire path-of-travel upgrade regime for alterations, forming a unified compliance framework with cost balancing provisions.

hyperedges.label: Residential Dwelling Unit Accessibility Framework
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 11B-233 (public housing scoping) and 11B-809 (technical requirements) combined with mobility and adaptable feature concepts form the complete residential dwelling unit accessibility framework applied across all public housing construction.

hyperedges.label: Emergency Sleeping Cabin Life Safety Requirements
hyperedges.rationale: Sections P104.4 (egress), P104.8 (smoke alarms), and P104.9 (CO alarms) collectively form the life-safety egress and alarm requirement set for emergency sleeping cabins.

hyperedges.label: Loft Access and Egress Options
hyperedges.rationale: Sections P108.2.1 through P108.2.4 collectively define the permissible loft access and safety guard options for emergency housing lofts.

hyperedges.label: Dependent Unit Sanitation Facility Requirements
hyperedges.rationale: Sections P110.2, P110.3, and P110.4 together form the sanitation and waste management requirements for dependent unit occupants in emergency housing sites.

hyperedges.label: Seismic Analysis Suite: Loading + Structural Performance + Component Design
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 3103F.4, 3104F, and 3107F together define the complete seismic analysis workflow: earthquake loads/parameters → two-level performance criteria and analytical procedures → material strain limits and component capacity for MOT structures.

hyperedges.label: Audit-Rating-Action Triad: Inspection Scope + Assessment Ratings + Follow-up Actions
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 3102F.3 (audit scope), Table 31F-2-4 (assessment ratings OSAR/SSAR/ICAR), and Table 31F-2-5 (RAP remedial priorities) form an integrated compliance framework for evaluating and acting on MOT condition.

hyperedges.label: Mooring System: Environmental Loads + Mooring Analysis + Hardware Design
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 3103F.5 (environmental forces on vessels), 3105F.2 (mooring analysis procedures), and 3105F.8 (mooring hardware sizing and safety factors) together constitute the complete mooring system design requirement chain.

hyperedges.label: Lateral Force-Resisting System Design Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 2305, 2306.2, and 2306.3 together govern the complete design of wood-frame lateral force-resisting systems: 2305 establishes the general design requirements and references AWC SDPWS, 2306.2 provides diaphragm-specific allowable shear values, and 2306.3 provides shear wall allowable shear values — all must be satisfied together for a code-compliant LFRS.

hyperedges.label: Wood Truss Design, Submittal, and Quality Assurance Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 2303.4.1, 2303.4.1.2, and 2303.4.1.3 collectively establish the complete truss design requirements: design drawing content (2303.4.1), permanent restraint methods (2303.4.1.2), and registered design professional requirements for long-span trusses ≥60 ft (2303.4.1.3).

hyperedges.label: Wood Decay and Termite Protection Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Section 2304.12 (protection requirements by location), 2303.1.9 (preservative-treated wood standards and labeling), and AWPA U1 collectively form the complete wood protection system — identifying where, what treatment standard applies, and how treated material must be identified.

hyperedges.label: High-Rise Building Life Safety System Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 403.3, 403.4.7, 403.4.8, 403.5.4, and 403.6.1 together constitute the integrated life safety system requirements—sprinklers, smoke control, emergency power, smokeproof enclosures, and fire service elevators—that collectively define high-rise fire protection strategy

hyperedges.label: Group I-2 Smoke Compartmentation and Egress Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 407.5, 407.5.1, 407.6, and 407.7 together define the defend-in-place strategy for I-2 occupancies: smoke barriers subdivide floors into compartments, automatic-closing doors restrict smoke movement, and sprinklers protect throughout—all required simultaneously

hyperedges.label: Group H-5 Fabrication Area Safety Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 415.11.1, 415.11.1.1, 415.11.2, and 415.11.3 together form the H-5 semiconductor fabrication safety framework: quantity limits per fabrication area, HPM restrictions in corridors, and separate service corridors for HPM transport

hyperedges.label: Occupant Load to Egress Sizing Pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: These three sections form an integrated requirement: occupant load is calculated per Table 1004.5, that load drives required egress capacity per Section 1005.3 (width = OL x capacity factor), and the occupant load also determines the number of exits required per Section 1006.2.1 and Table 1006.2.1.

hyperedges.label: Three-Part Means of Egress System
hyperedges.rationale: Exit access (Sections 1016-1021), exit (Sections 1022-1027), and exit discharge (Sections 1028-1029) together constitute the complete means of egress pathway required by Section 1001.1; each part has its own dimensional, fire-resistance, and signage requirements.

hyperedges.label: Accessible Means of Egress and Refuge System
hyperedges.rationale: These sections collectively govern accessible means of egress: Section 1009.1 requires accessible means of egress from each accessible space, Section 1009.3 specifies accessible stairway requirements (48-inch clear width), and Section 1009.6 establishes area of refuge requirements (size, separation, two-way communication) as the shelter-in-place component of the accessible egress strategy.

hyperedges.label: Occupancy-Based Sprinkler Trigger Thresholds
hyperedges.rationale: These sections collectively define fire area thresholds (5,000–24,000 sq ft) and occupant load thresholds (100–300) that trigger sprinkler requirements for various occupancy groups, forming a coherent threshold-based requirement system.

hyperedges.label: High-Rise Building Integrated Fire Protection Requirements
hyperedges.rationale: For high-rise buildings (occupied floors >75 ft above lowest fire department vehicle access), these sections together mandate automatic smoke detection, emergency voice/alarm communication system, fire command center, zoning annunciator panel, and firefighter smoke control panel—a unified heightened protection system.

hyperedges.label: Smoke Control Method Alternatives
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 909.6, 909.7, and 909.8 define the three permitted mechanical smoke control design methods—pressurization, airflow, and exhaust—which collectively constitute the complete set of code-recognized approaches for mechanical smoke control.

hyperedges.label: Accessible Parking System (Percentage, Location, Design)
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1109A.3 (required quantity), 1109A.7 (location criteria), and 1109A.8 (design/construction standards) together form the complete accessible parking requirement framework for covered multifamily dwellings.

hyperedges.label: Primary Entry Door Accessibility System
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1132A.1 (width/height), 1132A.5 (maneuvering clearances), and 1132A.8 (hardware) together define the complete accessible primary entry door system for covered multifamily dwelling units.

hyperedges.label: Building Permit Process: Application → Plan Review → Permit Issuance → Inspections → Certificate of Occupancy
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 105.3, 107, 105.1, 110, and 111 together form the complete building permit lifecycle from application through certificate of occupancy issuance.

hyperedges.label: State Agency Enforcement Matrix: BSC → DSA/OSHPD/SFM/HCD → Enforcing Agency → Local Jurisdiction
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1.2 through 1.14 establish a layered enforcement hierarchy where BSC oversees adoption, specialized state agencies enforce within their scope, and local jurisdictions fill remaining authority.

hyperedges.label: Code Enforcement Appeals: Violation Notice → Stop Work Order → Board of Appeals → Prosecution

hyperedges.label: Seismic Design Parameter Chain
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1613.2.1 through 1613.2.5 form the mandatory sequential chain for seismic design: mapped Ss/S1 → site-adjusted SMS/SM1 → design SDS/SD1 → Seismic Design Category assignment.

hyperedges.label: Wind Design Parameter Chain
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1609.3, 1609.3.1, and 1609.4 together form the wind design parameter chain: determine basic design wind speed V by risk category → convert to Vasd where needed → assign exposure category for final wind pressure calculation.

hyperedges.label: Expansive Soil Investigation-Design-Construction Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: These three sections form a complete requirement chain: 1803.5.3 defines and requires testing for expansive soil; 1808.6 mandates design approaches for foundations on expansive soils; 1808.6.2 provides slab-on-ground design methodology via WRI/CRSI and PTI DC 10.5.

hyperedges.label: Seismic Geotechnical Investigation Requirement Set (SDC C-F)
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1803.5.11, 1803.5.12, and 1803.6 collectively define what seismic hazard evaluations are required and how they must be reported for SDC C through F structures.

hyperedges.label: Deep Foundation Design-Detailing-Installation Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1810.2 (analysis), 1810.3 (design/detailing), and 1810.4 (installation) form an integrated deep foundation requirement set that must be satisfied together.

hyperedges.label: Geotechnical Investigation — Report — Peer Review Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1803A.5 (investigation conditions), 1803A.7 (reporting requirements), and 1803A.8 (peer review) together form a complete investigation-to-approval workflow for DSA-SS/CC projects.

hyperedges.label: Seismic Deep Foundation Design Set — SDC D-F
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1810A.2.4.1 (curvature demands), 1810A.3.6.1 (seismic splice requirements), and 1810A.3.9.4 (seismic reinforcement) together form the SDC D-F seismic detailing requirement set for deep foundations.

hyperedges.label: Expansive Soil Identification and Foundation Design Set
hyperedges.rationale: Section 1803A.5.3 (identification criteria using ASTM tests), 1808A.6.1 (structural foundation design), and 1808A.6.2 (slab-on-ground design) together form the complete expansive soil mitigation chain from identification through design.

hyperedges.label: Structural Steel Seismic Inspection Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1705A.2.1 (quality assurance), 1705A.13.1 (seismic special inspections for SDC D-F), and 1705A.14 (nondestructive testing) together form the complete structural steel seismic inspection requirement set, all invoking AISC 341 Chapter J/N with California modifications.

hyperedges.label: Sprayed Fire-Resistant Material Complete Inspection Set
hyperedges.rationale: Section 1705A.15 together with ASTM E605 (thickness and density) and ASTM E736 (bond strength) form an inseparable inspection triad; all three must be satisfied to comply with SFRM special inspection requirements for floor, roof, wall and structural member applications.

hyperedges.label: Concrete Quality Control Inspection Triad
hyperedges.rationale: The batch plant inspection section (1705A.3.3), the comprehensive concrete inspection table (Table 1705A.3 including specimen fabrication per ASTM C31/C172), and ASTM C94 certification pathway together constitute the complete concrete quality control inspection system for OSHPD/DSA projects.

nodes.rationale: Governs materials, systems and assemblies for structural fire resistance and fire-resistance-rated construction to safeguard against spread of fire and smoke.

nodes.rationale: Fire-resistance rating determined without automatic sprinklers unless Section 703.2.3 applies.

nodes.label: 703.2.1 Tested Assemblies
nodes.rationale: Fire-resistance rating of building elements determined by ASTM E119 or UL 263 test procedures.

nodes.label: 703.6 Noncombustible Protection Time Contribution
nodes.rationale: Time in minutes contributed by noncombustible protection of mass timber established by comparison of assemblies tested per ASTM E119 or UL 263.

nodes.label: 1201.1 Scope
nodes.rationale: Governs ventilation, temperature control, lighting, yards and courts, sound transmission, room dimensions, surrounding materials and rodentproofing for interior spaces of buildings.

nodes.label: 1202.1 General Ventilation
nodes.rationale: Buildings shall be provided with natural ventilation per Section 1202.5, or mechanical ventilation per California Mechanical Code.

nodes.label: 1202.2.1 Ventilated Attics and Rafter Spaces
nodes.rationale: Net free ventilating area shall be not less than 1/150 of the area of the space ventilated. Can be reduced to 1/300 if climate-zone vapor retarder installed and 40-50% of required venting in upper portion.

nodes.label: 1202.2.2 Openings into Attic
nodes.rationale: Exterior openings into attic shall be protected against entry of birds, squirrels, rodents, snakes. Openings for ventilation with least dimension over 1/4 inch shall have corrosion-resistant wire cloth screening.

nodes.label: 1202.3 Unvented Attic and Unvented Enclosed Rafter Assemblies
nodes.rationale: Permitted when attic space is completely within building thermal envelope, no interior Class I vapor retarders on ceiling side, and insulation meets condensation control R-values per Table 1202.3. Does not apply to special use structures (pools, data centers, hospitals, art galleries).
nodes.norm_label: 1202.3 unvented attic and unvented enclosed rafter assemblies

nodes.rationale: IECC climate zones differ from California Energy Code climate zones. Comparison shown in Table 1202.3.1.

nodes.label: 1202.4 Under-Floor Ventilation
nodes.rationale: Space between floor joists and earth under buildings (except basements/cellars) shall be ventilated per Section 1202.4.1, 1202.4.2 or 1202.4.3.

nodes.label: 1202.4.1 Ventilation Openings
nodes.rationale: Openings through foundation walls shall provide cross ventilation. Covers must have least dimension not greater than 1/4 inch.

nodes.label: 1202.4.1.1 Ventilation Area for Crawl Spaces with Open Earth Floors
nodes.rationale: Net area of ventilation openings not less than 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft of crawl space area.
nodes.norm_label: 1202.4.1.1 ventilation area for crawl spaces with open earth floors

nodes.label: 1202.4.1.2 Ventilation Area for Crawl Spaces with Covered Floors
nodes.rationale: When ground surface covered with Class I vapor retarder, net area not less than 1 sq ft per 1,500 sq ft of crawl space area.
nodes.norm_label: 1202.4.1.2 ventilation area for crawl spaces with covered floors

nodes.label: 1202.4.3 Mechanical Ventilation for Crawl Spaces
nodes.rationale: Required where ground surface covered with Class I vapor retarder.

nodes.label: 1202.4.3.1 Continuous Mechanical Ventilation
nodes.rationale: Rate of 1.0 cfm per 50 sq ft of crawl space ground surface area.

nodes.label: 1202.4.3.2 Conditioned Space Crawl Space
nodes.rationale: Crawl space conditioned per California Mechanical Code; walls insulated per California Energy Code.

nodes.label: 1202.4.4 Flood Hazard Areas
nodes.rationale: In flood hazard areas per Section 1612.3, under-floor ventilation openings deemed compliant with ASCE 24 flood opening requirements if designed per ASCE 24.

nodes.label: 1202.5 Natural Ventilation
nodes.rationale: Natural ventilation through windows, doors, louvers or other openings to outdoors. Operating mechanism shall provide ready access so occupants can control openings.

nodes.label: 1202.5.1 Ventilation Area Required
nodes.rationale: Openable area of openings to outdoors shall be not less than 4 percent of floor area being ventilated.

nodes.label: 1202.5.2.1 Bathrooms
nodes.rationale: Rooms containing bathtubs, showers, spas shall be mechanically ventilated per California Mechanical Code. Minimum exhaust rate per Table 403.7. Group R occupancies also per CALGreen Chapter 4, Division 4.5.

nodes.label: 1203.1 Temperature Control Equipment and Systems
nodes.rationale: Interior spaces for human occupancy shall have active or passive space heating systems capable of maintaining 68°F (20°C) at 3 feet above floor on design heating day. Exceptions: spaces not for human comfort, Group F/H/S/U occupancies.

nodes.label: 1204.1 General Lighting
nodes.rationale: Every space for human occupancy shall have natural light per Section 1204.2 or artificial light per Section 1204.3.

nodes.label: 1204.2 Natural Light
nodes.rationale: Minimum net glazed area not less than 8 percent of floor area of room served.

nodes.label: 1204.2.2 Exterior Openings
nodes.rationale: Exterior openings for natural light shall open directly onto a public way, yard or court per Section 1205.

nodes.label: 1204.3 Artificial Light
nodes.rationale: Artificial light shall provide average illumination of 10 footcandles (107 lux) over area of room at 30 inches above floor.

nodes.label: 1204.4 Stairway Illumination
nodes.rationale: Stairways within dwelling units and exterior stairways serving dwelling units shall have illumination level on tread runs of not less than 1 footcandle (11 lux).

nodes.label: 1204.7 Campus Lighting for Parking Facilities
nodes.rationale: Applies to California State Universities, colleges and community colleges (not UC unless Regents adopt).

nodes.label: 1205.1 Yards or Courts General
nodes.rationale: Yards and courts adjacent to exterior openings providing natural light or ventilation shall be on the same lot as the building.

nodes.label: 1205.2 Yards
nodes.rationale: Yards shall be not less than 3 feet wide for buildings 2 stories or less. Increase 1 foot per additional story. For buildings over 14 stories, compute based on 14 stories.

nodes.label: 1205.3 Courts
nodes.rationale: Courts not less than 3 feet wide; 6 feet when windows open on opposite sides; not less than 10 feet long unless bounded by public way or yard. Increase 1 foot width / 2 feet length per additional story above 2.

nodes.label: 1205.3.2 Air Intake
nodes.rationale: Courts more than two stories in height shall have horizontal air intake at bottom not less than 10 sq ft leading to exterior unless abutting yard or public way.

nodes.label: 1205.3.3 Court Drainage
nodes.rationale: Bottom of every court shall be graded and drained to public sewer or approved disposal system per California Plumbing Code.

nodes.label: 1206.1 Sound Transmission Scope
nodes.rationale: Applies to common interior walls, partitions and floor/ceiling assemblies between adjacent dwelling units and sleeping units or between dwelling/sleeping units and adjacent public areas.

nodes.label: 1206.2 Airborne Sound
nodes.rationale: Sound transmission class of not less than 50 per ASTM E90, or NNIC rating of not less than 45 per ASTM E336.

nodes.label: 1206.2.1 Masonry Sound Transmission
nodes.rationale: STC of concrete masonry and clay masonry assemblies shall be calculated per TMS 302 or determined through ASTM E90 testing.

nodes.label: 1206.3 Structure-Borne Sound
nodes.rationale: Floor-ceiling assemblies between dwelling/sleeping units shall have IIC rating of not less than 50 per ASTM E492, or NISR of not less than 45 per ASTM E1007.

nodes.label: 1206.4 Allowable Interior Noise Levels
nodes.rationale: Interior noise levels from exterior sources shall not exceed 45 dB in any habitable room. Metric is Ldn or CNEL consistent with local general plan noise element.

nodes.label: 1207.1 Enhanced Classroom Acoustics General
nodes.rationale: Enhanced classroom acoustics shall comply with Section 808 of ICC A117.1.

nodes.label: 1207.2 Enhanced Classroom Acoustics Where Required
nodes.rationale: Required in Group E occupancies for all classrooms with volume of 20,000 cubic feet or less.

nodes.label: 1208.1 Minimum Room Widths
nodes.rationale: Habitable spaces other than kitchens shall be not less than 7 feet in any plan dimension. Kitchens shall have clear passageway of not less than 3 feet between counter fronts and appliances or walls.

nodes.label: 1208.2 Minimum Ceiling Heights
nodes.rationale: Occupiable spaces, habitable spaces and corridors: not less than 7 feet 6 inches. Bathrooms, toilet rooms, kitchens, storage and laundry rooms: not less than 7 feet. Exceptions for beams, sloped ceilings, mezzanines, dwelling unit corridors.

nodes.label: 1208.3 Room Area
nodes.rationale: Every dwelling unit shall have at least one room with not less than 120 sq ft net floor area. Other habitable rooms shall have not less than 70 sq ft.

nodes.label: 1208.4 Efficiency Dwelling Units
nodes.rationale: Living room not less than 190 sq ft; separate closet required; kitchen sink, cooking appliance and refrigerator; separate bathroom with water closet, lavatory and bathtub or shower.

nodes.label: 1209.1 Crawl Spaces Access
nodes.rationale: Crawl spaces shall be provided with at least one access opening not less than 18 by 24 inches.

nodes.label: 1209.2 Attic Spaces Access
nodes.rationale: Opening not less than 20 by 30 inches to any attic with clear height over 30 inches. Clear headroom not less than 30 inches at or above the access opening.

nodes.label: 1210.2 Finish Materials for Toilet and Bathrooms
nodes.norm_label: 1210.2 finish materials for toilet and bathrooms

nodes.label: 1210.2.3 Showers
nodes.rationale: Shower compartments and walls above bathtubs with shower heads shall be finished with smooth, nonabsorbent surface to height not less than 72 inches above drain inlet.

nodes.label: 1210.3 Privacy for Public Restrooms
nodes.rationale: Public restrooms shall be visually screened from outside entry or exit doorways. Exception for single-occupant rooms with lockable door.

nodes.label: 1210.3.1 Water Closet Compartment
nodes.rationale: Each water closet used by public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls/partitions and door.

nodes.label: 1210.3.2 Urinal Partitions
nodes.rationale: Each urinal used by public or employees shall have partitions beginning not more than 12 inches from floor and extending not less than 60 inches above finished floor.

nodes.label: 1211.1 Garage Door Springs General
nodes.rationale: Applies to HCD 1 and HCD 2 regulated applications. Extension springs must conform to ASTM A227/A227M-17 (hard-drawn) or ASTM A229/A229M-17 (oil-tempered).

nodes.label: 1211.4 Restraining Devices for Garage Door Springs
nodes.rationale: Each extension spring shall have a restraining device tested per ANSI/DASMA 103-2017 or equivalent.
nodes.norm_label: 1211.4 restraining devices for garage door springs

nodes.label: 1212.1 Finish Material Pollutant Control
nodes.rationale: Adhesives, sealants, paints, coatings, carpet systems, composite wood products shall meet VOC emission limits per CALGreen Chapter 4, Division 4.5.

nodes.label: 1224.1 Scope - Hospitals (OSHPD 1)
nodes.rationale: Applies to general acute-care hospitals and those providing only acute medical rehabilitation center services.

nodes.label: 1224.4.6.1 Station Outlets
nodes.rationale: Station outlets for oxygen, vacuum and medical air shall comply with Table 1224.4.6.1.

nodes.label: 1224.4.6.2 Gas and Vacuum Systems
nodes.rationale: Design, installation and testing of medical gas and vacuum systems shall conform to Table 1224.4.6.1 and NFPA 99.

nodes.label: 1224.4.6.3 Hyperbaric Facilities
nodes.rationale: Design and construction shall conform to NFPA 99 and Section 1224.39.5.

nodes.label: 1224.4.7 Corridors (OSHPD)
nodes.rationale: Minimum width of corridors and hallways shall be 8 feet. Psychiatric care corridors for non-bedridden patients: minimum 6 feet clear.

nodes.label: 1224.4.10 Ceiling Heights (OSHPD)
nodes.rationale: Minimum ceiling height 8 feet. Closets, toilet rooms: not less than 7 feet.

nodes.label: 1224.14.1 Patient Rooms
nodes.rationale: No more than 4 beds per room. New construction: 100 sq ft per bed (multiple-bed) or 120 sq ft (single-bed) clear floor area. Minimum 3 feet clearance around bed sides and foot.

nodes.label: 1224.14.3 Airborne Infection Isolation Rooms
nodes.rationale: Ratio of one isolation room per 35 licensed beds. Must have anteroom, labeled 'Airborne Infection Room', sealed-tight perimeter.

nodes.label: 1224.15 Surgical Service Space
nodes.rationale: Divided into semi-restricted and restricted areas. Number of operating rooms in ratio to licensed bed capacity: <25 beds=1 OR, 25-99=2 OR, 100+= 3 OR.

nodes.label: 1224.15.2.1 General Operating Room
nodes.rationale: Minimum clear floor area of 400 sq ft with minimum 20 feet clear dimension between fixed cabinets.

nodes.label: 1224.16 Anesthesia/Recovery Service Space
nodes.rationale: Shall provide perioperative support services. Located adjacent to surgical service space with direct access to semi-restricted corridor.

nodes.label: 1224.17 Clinical Laboratory Service Space
nodes.rationale: All hospitals shall provide space for urinalysis, complete blood counts, hemoglobin blood typing and cross matching.

nodes.rationale: Specifies minimum R-values of air-impermeable insulation by IECC climate zone: 2B/3B tile=0, 1/2A/2B/3A/3B/3C=R-5, 4C=R-10, 4A/4B=R-15, 5=R-20, 6=R-25, 7=R-30, 8=R-35.

nodes.label: Airborne Infection Isolation Room
nodes.rationale: A single-occupancy patient room where environmental factors are controlled to minimize transmission of infectious agents spread by droplet nuclei.

nodes.label: Protective Environment Room
nodes.rationale: A bedded unit or patient room for severely immunosuppressed patients.

nodes.label: 11B-101 Purpose
nodes.rationale: Establishes scope: scoping and technical requirements for accessibility to sites, facilities, buildings and elements by individuals with disabilities, applied during design, construction, additions and alterations.

nodes.label: 11B-103 Equivalent Facilitation
nodes.rationale: Permits alternative designs, products or technologies that result in substantially equivalent or greater accessibility and usability.

nodes.label: 11B-201 Application
nodes.rationale: All areas of newly designed and newly constructed buildings and facilities and altered portions of existing buildings shall comply.

nodes.label: 11B-202 Existing Buildings and Facilities
nodes.rationale: Governs additions and alterations to existing buildings. Alterations must comply; technically infeasible situations allow equivalent facilitation. Prohibits reduction in access.

nodes.label: 11B-202.4 Path of Travel Requirements in Alterations
nodes.rationale: Requires accessible path of travel to altered areas, including primary entrance, toilet and bathing facilities, drinking fountains, telephones, and signs. Cost limited to 20% of adjusted construction cost for projects below valuation threshold.
nodes.norm_label: 11b-202.4 path of travel requirements in alterations

nodes.label: 11B-206 Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Central scoping provision requiring accessible routes to connect site arrival points, within sites, between stories, to spaces and elements, and to entrances.

nodes.label: 11B-206.2.3 Multistory Buildings and Facilities
nodes.rationale: Requires accessible route connecting each story and mezzanine. Private-funded multistory buildings under 3 stories or under 3000 sq ft per story may be exempt.

nodes.label: 11B-206.4 Entrances
nodes.rationale: All entrances shall comply with Section 11B-404 and be on an accessible route.

nodes.label: 11B-206.7 Platform Lifts
nodes.rationale: Platform lifts permitted as accessible route components in specific circumstances including performance areas, incidental spaces, judicial spaces, existing site constraints, guest rooms, amusement rides, play areas, and recreational boating.

nodes.label: 11B-208 Parking Spaces
nodes.rationale: Scoping for accessible parking spaces by facility type. Hospital outpatient=10%, rehabilitation=20%, residential=by unit. Van spaces required at 1 per 6 accessible spaces.

nodes.label: 11B-211 Drinking Fountains and Bottle-Filling Stations
nodes.rationale: Minimum two drinking fountains required; one high-reach and one low-reach. Where more than minimum, 50% each type.

nodes.label: 11B-213 Toilet Facilities and Bathing Facilities
nodes.rationale: Each toilet and bathing room must comply with 11B-603. Toilet compartments: min 5% comply with 11B-604.8.1; water closets min 5%; urinals min 10%; lavatories min 10%.

nodes.label: 11B-216 Signs
nodes.rationale: Requires accessible signs at permanent rooms/spaces (Braille + raised characters), egress, parking, entrances, toilet/bathing rooms, elevators, TTYs, assistive listening systems.

nodes.label: 11B-219 Assistive Listening Systems
nodes.rationale: Required in assembly areas with fixed seating accommodating 50+ persons or with audio amplification. 4% of seats as receivers, minimum 2; 25% hearing-aid compatible.

nodes.label: 11B-221 Assembly Areas
nodes.rationale: Assembly areas must provide wheelchair spaces, companion seats, designated aisle seats (5% of aisle seats) and semi-ambulant seats (1% of total, min 2). Dispersion required horizontally and vertically.

nodes.label: Table 11B-221.2.1.1 Number of Wheelchair Spaces in Assembly Areas

nodes.label: 11B-224 Transient Lodging Guest Rooms
nodes.rationale: Hotels, motels and similar facilities must provide guest rooms with mobility features and communication features per tables. Rooms must be dispersed by class.

nodes.label: Table 11B-224.2 Guest Rooms with Mobility Features
nodes.rationale: Specifies minimum rooms without roll-in showers and with roll-in showers by total guest room count.
nodes.norm_label: table 11b-224.2 guest rooms with mobility features

nodes.label: 11B-228.3 Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
nodes.rationale: EVCS scoping by charging level and connector type. Van accessible, standard accessible, and ambulatory accessible EVCS required per Table 11B-228.3.2.1.

nodes.label: Table 11B-228.3.2.1 Electric Vehicle Charging Stations for Public Use
nodes.norm_label: table 11b-228.3.2.1 electric vehicle charging stations for public use

nodes.label: 11B-233 Public Housing Facilities
nodes.rationale: At least 5% of residential dwelling units must have mobility features, at least 2% communication features. Adaptable features required for elevator buildings and ground floor non-elevator buildings.

nodes.label: 11B-247 Detectable Warnings and Detectable Directional Texture
nodes.rationale: Detectable warnings required at platform edges, curb ramps, islands/medians, bus stops, blended transitions, reflecting pools, and track crossings.
nodes.norm_label: 11b-247 detectable warnings and detectable directional texture

nodes.label: 11B-250 Circulation Paths
nodes.rationale: Circulation paths contiguous to vehicular traffic must be physically separated by being raised 4 inches minimum above vehicular area.

nodes.label: 11B-302 Floor or Ground Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Floor and ground surfaces must be stable, firm and slip resistant. Carpet pile height max 1/2 inch. Openings max 1/2 inch diameter.

nodes.label: 11B-303 Changes in Level
nodes.rationale: Vertical changes max 1/4 inch; beveled up to 1/2 inch at max 1:2 slope; greater changes require ramp. Warning curbs required for abrupt drops over 4 inches.

nodes.label: 11B-304 Turning Space
nodes.rationale: Circular 60-inch diameter or T-shaped space within 60-inch square with 36-inch arms required for wheelchair turning.

nodes.label: 11B-305 Clear Floor or Ground Space
nodes.rationale: 30 inches x 48 inches minimum clear floor space for forward or parallel approach. Max 1:48 slope. Maneuvering clearances required in alcoves.

nodes.label: 11B-307 Protruding Objects
nodes.rationale: Objects with leading edges 27 to 80 inches above floor protrude max 4 inches into circulation path. Vertical clearance 80 inches minimum.

nodes.label: 11B-308 Reach Ranges
nodes.rationale: Forward reach: high 48 inches max, low 15 inches min. Side reach same. Obstructed high forward reach limited to 44 inches if depth >20 inches.

nodes.label: 11B-309 Operable Parts
nodes.rationale: Operable with one hand, no tight grasping/pinching/twisting. Max 5 lbs activation force. Must be within reach ranges.

nodes.label: 11B-402 Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Components: walking surfaces at max 1:20 slope, doorways, ramps, curb ramps, elevators, platform lifts.

nodes.label: 11B-403 Walking Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Running slope max 1:20, cross slope max 1:48. Clear width 36 inches min (48 inches for sidewalks). Passing spaces every 200 feet where width < 60 inches.

nodes.label: 11B-404 Doors, Doorways and Gates
nodes.rationale: Manual doors: 32-inch min clear width; maneuvering clearances per table; max 1/2-inch threshold; 5 lb max opening force for interior; hardware at 34-44 inches. Automatic doors comply with BHMA A156.10 or A156.19.

nodes.label: 11B-404.2 Manual Doors, Doorways and Manual Gates
nodes.norm_label: 11b-404.2 manual doors, doorways and manual gates

nodes.label: 11B-404.2.3 Clear Width
nodes.rationale: 32 inches minimum clear width; 36 inches for openings more than 24 inches deep. No projections below 34 inches; projections 34-80 inches max 4 inches.

nodes.label: Table 11B-404.2.4.1 Maneuvering Clearances at Manual Swinging Doors
nodes.rationale: Front-pull=60x18 inches; Front-push=48x0 inches; hinge-pull=60x36 inches; latch-pull=60x24 inches.
nodes.norm_label: table 11b-404.2.4.1 maneuvering clearances at manual swinging doors

nodes.label: 11B-405 Ramps
nodes.rationale: Max 1:12 running slope; max 1:48 cross slope; min 48-inch clear width; max 30-inch rise per run. Landings 60x60 inches min (top 60 wide, bottom 72 long). Handrails and edge protection required.

nodes.label: 11B-406 Curb Ramps, Blended Transitions and Islands
nodes.rationale: Perpendicular: max 1:12 slope; flares max 1:10. Parallel: in-line with sidewalk direction. Blended transitions: max 1:20. All require detectable warnings. Min 48-inch clear width.
nodes.norm_label: 11b-406 curb ramps, blended transitions and islands

nodes.label: 11B-407 Elevators
nodes.rationale: Passenger elevators must comply with ASME A17.1. Automatic operation required. Car dimensions, controls, signals, hall signals, door reopening devices, and emergency communications all specified.

nodes.label: Table 11B-407.4.1 Elevator Car Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Centered door: 42-inch door, 80x51x54 inside. Side door: 36-inch door, 68x51x54. Any: 36-inch door, 54x80x80 or 60x60x60 with turning space.

nodes.label: 11B-410 Platform Lifts
nodes.rationale: Platform lifts comply with ASME A18.1. Unassisted entry/exit required. Low-energy power-operated doors. Landing size 60x60 inches minimum.

nodes.label: 11B-411 Destination-Oriented Elevators
nodes.rationale: Comply with ASME A17.1. Numeric floor designations. Hall call consoles with touch screen or keypad, accessibility function button (International Symbol of Accessibility), audio output.

nodes.label: 11B-812 Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
nodes.rationale: Technical requirements for accessible EVCS including van accessible, standard accessible, and ambulatory accessible configurations.

nodes.rationale: Space required at doors and gates to allow wheelchair users to maneuver for opening. Dimensions vary by approach direction and pull/push side per Table 11B-404.2.4.1.

nodes.label: Concept: Accessible Route
nodes.rationale: Continuous unobstructed path connecting accessible elements, complying with Division 4 technical requirements.

nodes.label: Concept: Path of Travel (Alteration Requirement)
nodes.rationale: When alterations occur, path of travel to altered area including entrance, toilets, drinking fountains, phones and signs must be made accessible, subject to 20% cost cap.

nodes.label: Concept: Mobility Features (Residential)
nodes.rationale: Full accessibility features for residential dwelling units per Sections 11B-809.2 through 11B-809.4.

nodes.label: Concept: Adaptable Features (Residential)
nodes.rationale: Features that can be added or modified to provide accessibility without extensive structural changes, per Sections 11B-809.6 through 11B-809.12.

nodes.label: Concept: Valuation Threshold (Path of Travel Cost Cap)
nodes.rationale: Dollar threshold for determining whether 20% cost cap applies or whether unreasonable hardship findings can be made for path-of-travel requirements.

nodes.rationale: 1-200 spaces: 5% min 1; 201+: 10 plus 2% over 200.

nodes.rationale: Toe clearance: floor to 9 inches, max 25-inch depth. Knee clearance: 9 to 27 inches above floor; min 11-inch depth at 9-inch height. Both 30 inches wide minimum.

nodes.label: Appendix P Emergency Housing
nodes.rationale: Appendix provisions are not mandatory unless specifically referenced in the adopting ordinance.

nodes.label: P101.1 Scope
nodes.rationale: Appendix is applicable to emergency housing and emergency housing facilities as defined in Section P102.

nodes.label: P102.1 General Definitions
nodes.rationale: References Chapter 2 of CBC for general definitions.

nodes.label: P103.1 General
nodes.rationale: Emergency sleeping cabins, transportable housing units, membrane structures and tents shall be occupied only during declared emergency or shelter crisis. Buildings per CBSC may be permanently occupied.

nodes.label: P103.2 Existing Buildings
nodes.rationale: Existing buildings may be used as emergency housing if complying with code in effect at original construction; shall not become substandard as determined by enforcing agency.

nodes.label: P103.2.1 New Additions, Alterations and Change of Occupancy
nodes.rationale: Exception allows existing buildings used for emergency housing to not comply with California Energy Code if determined by enforcing agency.
nodes.norm_label: p103.2.1 new additions, alterations and change of occupancy

nodes.label: P103.3 Occupant Load
nodes.rationale: Minimum 70 sf for first occupant, 50 sf per additional occupant. Exception allows reduction to 53 sf for single-occupancy sleeping unit if enforcing agency approves.

nodes.label: P103.4 Fire and Life Safety Requirements Not Addressed in This Appendix
nodes.rationale: Fire and life safety measures not addressed here are determined and enforced by the enforcing agency.
nodes.norm_label: p103.4 fire and life safety requirements not addressed in this appendix

nodes.label: P104.1 General
nodes.rationale: Minimum 70 sf interior floor area for one occupant; 50 sf per additional; maximum 400 sf excluding lofts.

nodes.label: P104.2 Live Loads
nodes.rationale: Floor live load 40 psf; horizontal live load 15 psf; roof live load 20 psf; snow loads where greater than 20 psf must be accommodated.

nodes.label: P104.3 Minimum Ceiling Height
nodes.rationale: Habitable space and hallways 80 inches; bathrooms/kitchens 76 inches. Exception for lofts per Section P108.

nodes.label: P104.4 Means of Egress
nodes.rationale: At least two forms of egress placed remotely; when loft provided one egress must be an egress window in the loft space.

nodes.label: P104.4.1 Egress Window
nodes.rationale: Sill max 44 in above floor; min 24 in height, 20 in width, 5 sf net clear opening area.

nodes.label: P104.6 Electrical
nodes.rationale: Requires continuous electricity, at least one interior lighting fixture, electrical heating with dedicated receptacle (or nonelectrical alternative), at least one GFCI-protected receptacle.

nodes.label: P104.9 Carbon Monoxide Alarms
nodes.rationale: Required only when fuel-burning appliance(s) or fireplace(s) are present.

nodes.label: P105.1 General
nodes.rationale: Manufactured homes, mobilehomes, multifamily manufactured homes, commercial modulars, RVs and park trailers must comply with Health and Safety Code Division 13 Part 2 and Title 25 Division 1 Chapter 3 Subchapter 2.

nodes.label: P106.1 General
nodes.rationale: Tents must not house occupants more than 7 days unless with raised wooden floors or concrete slabs. A tent is not suitable sleeping when heating is required to maintain 50°F.

nodes.label: P107.1 General Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Emergency housing shall comply with Chapter 11B and/or US Access Board Final Guidelines for Emergency Transportable Housing (issued May 7, 2014, amending 2004 ADAAG and ABAAG).

nodes.label: P108.1 Minimum Loft Area and Dimensions
nodes.norm_label: p108.1 minimum loft area and dimensions

nodes.label: P108.1.1 Minimum Area
nodes.rationale: Minimum 35 sf floor area for lofts.

nodes.label: P108.1.2 Minimum Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Lofts shall be not less than 5 feet in any horizontal dimension.

nodes.label: P108.1.3 Height Effect on Loft Area
nodes.rationale: Portions with sloping ceiling less than 3 ft from floor not counted toward minimum area; exception for gable roofs with 6:12 slope: 16 inches threshold.
nodes.norm_label: p108.1.3 height effect on loft area

nodes.label: P108.2.1 Stairways
nodes.rationale: Stairways accessing lofts shall comply with California Residential Code or with Sections P108.2.1.1 through P108.2.1.6.

nodes.label: P108.2.1.1 Width
nodes.rationale: Minimum 17 inches at/above handrail; 20 inches below handrail.

nodes.label: P108.2.1.2 Headroom
nodes.rationale: Minimum 74 inches headroom measured vertically from sloped line connecting nosings.

nodes.label: P108.2.1.3 Treads and Risers
nodes.rationale: Risers 7–12 inches; tread/riser relationship determined by formula.

nodes.label: P108.2.1.4 Landing Platforms
nodes.rationale: Required when loft ceiling height less than 74 inches; depth 18–22 inches; height 16–18 inches above loft floor.

nodes.label: P108.2.2.1 Size and Capacity
nodes.rationale: Minimum 12-inch rung width; 10–14 inch rung spacing; 200 lb capacity per rung.

nodes.label: P108.2.2.2 Incline
nodes.rationale: Ladders installed at 70–80 degrees from horizontal.

nodes.label: P108.2.4 Loft Guards
nodes.rationale: Minimum 36 inches or half clear ceiling height, whichever is less; no sphere 4 inches diameter may pass through openings.

nodes.label: P109.1 Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Emergency housing and facilities shall be maintained safe, sanitary, and free from vermin and infectious matter; grounds kept clean.

nodes.label: P109.2 Identification
nodes.rationale: Address numbers/letters minimum 4 inches high, 0.5 inch wide, on contrasting background, facing street.

nodes.label: P110.2 Kitchens
nodes.rationale: Where dependent unit occupants cook for themselves, a common use kitchen with refrigerated storage is required.

nodes.label: P110.3 Toilet and Bathing Facilities
nodes.rationale: 1 toilet and 1 bathing facility per 15 occupants of each gender; bathing facilities must maintain 70°F; lavatories with running water adjacent to toilets.

nodes.label: P110.4 Garbage, Waste and Rubbish Disposal
nodes.norm_label: p110.4 garbage, waste and rubbish disposal

nodes.label: Declaration of Shelter Crisis
nodes.rationale: Proclaimed existence of situation where significant persons lack shelter threatening health/safety. See Government Code Section 8698.

nodes.label: Dependent Unit
nodes.rationale: Emergency housing without kitchen, toilet, and sewage disposal. Non-self-contained RVs without utility connections are dependent units.

nodes.label: Emergency Housing
nodes.rationale: Housing in permanent or temporary structure occupied during emergency or shelter crisis; includes buildings per CBSC, emergency sleeping cabins, emergency transportable housing units, and tents per this appendix.

nodes.label: Emergency Housing Facilities
nodes.rationale: On-site common use facilities supporting emergency housing; includes kitchen areas, toilets, showers, bathrooms with running water.

nodes.label: Emergency Sleeping Cabin
nodes.rationale: Relocatable hard-sided structure per this appendix; may only be occupied for emergency housing if allowed by enforcing agency.

nodes.label: Emergency Transportable Housing Unit
nodes.rationale: Single- or multiple-section prefabricated structure transportable by vehicle; includes manufactured homes, mobilehomes, multifamily manufactured homes, RVs, park trailers, and commercial modulars if approved. Does not include factory-built housing (HSC 19971).

nodes.label: Landing Platform
nodes.rationale: A landing provided as the top step of a stairway accessing a loft.

nodes.label: Local Emergency
nodes.rationale: Defined in Government Code Section 8558.

nodes.label: Loft
nodes.rationale: Floor level more than 30 inches above main floor; open on at least one side; ceiling height less than 6 ft 8 in; used as living or sleeping space.

nodes.label: Manufactured Home
nodes.rationale: Single-family dwelling per Health and Safety Code Section 18007.

nodes.label: Membrane Structure
nodes.rationale: Air-inflated, air-supported, cable or frame-covered structure; not otherwise defined as a tent. See Chapter 31.

nodes.label: Mobilehome
nodes.rationale: Single-family dwelling per Health and Safety Code Section 18008.

nodes.label: Multifamily Manufactured Home
nodes.rationale: Structure with not less than two dwelling units per Health and Safety Code Section 18008.7.

nodes.label: Park Trailer
nodes.rationale: Trailer for human habitation meeting Health and Safety Code Section 18009.3.

nodes.label: Recreational Vehicle
nodes.rationale: Motor home, travel trailer, truck camper or camping trailer designed for human habitation per Health and Safety Code Section 18010.

nodes.label: State of Emergency
nodes.rationale: Defined in Government Code Section 8558.

nodes.label: Tent
nodes.rationale: Structure/enclosure/shelter of fabric or pliable material supported by any means except by air or contents it protects.

nodes.label: 3101F Introduction
nodes.rationale: Establishes authority under California Public Resources Code 8750-8760; California State Lands Commission (SLC) regulates marine oil terminals (MOTs) to protect public health, safety and environment.

nodes.label: 3101F.1 Authority
nodes.rationale: Lempert-Keene-Seastrand Oil Spill Prevention and Response Act of 1990 authorizes SLC to regulate MOTs; Marine Environmental Protection Division administers this code.

nodes.label: 3101F.2 Purpose
nodes.rationale: Establishes minimum engineering, inspection and maintenance criteria for MOTs to prevent oil spills and protect public health, safety and the environment.

nodes.label: 3101F.3 Applicability
nodes.rationale: Classifies requirements as New (N), Existing (E), or Both (N/E); applies to all MOTs in California.

nodes.label: 3101F.5 Spill Prevention
nodes.rationale: Requires up-to-date Risk and Hazards Analysis per CCPS Guidelines; residual risks addressed by 2 CCR 2385.

nodes.label: 3101F.6 Oil Spill Exposure Classification
nodes.rationale: Categorizes MOTs as High, Moderate, or Low based on exposed oil volume, number of transfers per year, and maximum vessel size; uses ESD closure time formula.

nodes.label: 3101F.7 Management of Change
nodes.rationale: Requires MOC process per API Standard 2610 Section 6.6 whenever physical changes significantly impact operations.

nodes.label: 3101F.8 Review Requirements
nodes.rationale: Mandates quality assurance review, peer review for advanced analyses, and Division review for all audits and major changes.

nodes.label: 3102F Audit and Inspection
nodes.rationale: Defines minimum requirements for periodic audit and inspection of structural, mechanical, and electrical systems at MOTs.

nodes.label: 3102F.1.3 Berthing Systems
nodes.rationale: Defines berthing system as wharf and supporting structure, mechanical and electrical components, and pipeline systems that serve a berth; used for assigning structural ratings.

nodes.label: 3102F.3 Audits
nodes.rationale: Requires multidisciplinary team audit including above-water and underwater inspections, engineering evaluation, and recommended follow-up actions. Default 4-year audit interval.

nodes.label: 3102F.3.6 Evaluation and Assessment
nodes.rationale: Assigns OSAR, SSAR, and ICAR ratings; requires structural analysis including seismic per 3103F-3107F and mechanical/electrical evaluation per 3108F-3111F.

nodes.label: 3102F.4 Post-Event Inspection
nodes.rationale: Requires focused inspection after significant damage-causing events (earthquake, storm, vessel impact, fire, explosion, tsunami); action plan due within 5 days.

nodes.label: 3103F Structural Loading Criteria
nodes.rationale: Establishes environmental and operating loads acting on MOT structures and moored vessels; analysis procedures in 3104F-3107F.

nodes.label: 3103F.4 Earthquake Loads
nodes.rationale: Defines DPGA, DSA, DEM from USGS maps or site-specific PSHA; requires site amplification, near-fault directivity effects; site classes A-F; analysis dependent on spill classification.

nodes.label: 3103F.5 Mooring Loads on Vessels
nodes.rationale: Covers wind (OCIMF MEG3), current (NOAA, OCIMF MEG3), wave, passing vessel, seiche, and tsunami loads on moored vessels; 25-year return period for design wind.

nodes.label: 3103F.6 Berthing Loads
nodes.rationale: Quantifies berthing energy using kinetic energy formula with eccentricity, geometric, deformation, and configuration coefficients; based on UFC 4-152-01 and PIANC.

nodes.label: 3103F.7 Wind and Current Loads on Structures
nodes.rationale: Requires ASCE/SEI 7 Chapter 29 for wind loads on structure; current loads from Section 3103F.5.3 velocities.
nodes.norm_label: 3103f.7 wind and current loads on structures

nodes.label: 3103F.8 Load Combinations
nodes.rationale: Defines LRFD and ASD load combinations for vacant, mooring/breasting, berthing, and earthquake conditions per Tables 31F-3-10 and 31F-3-11.

nodes.label: 3104F Seismic Analysis and Structural Performance
nodes.rationale: Establishes two-level seismic performance criteria (Level 1 functionality, Level 2 major damage prevention); displacement-based nonlinear static (pushover) analysis required.

nodes.label: 3104F.2.1 Seismic Performance Criteria
nodes.rationale: Level 1: minor damage, no/temporary interruption; Level 2: controlled inelastic behavior, prevention of collapse and major spill. Return periods per Table 31F-4-1.

nodes.label: 3104F.2.3 Analytical Procedures
nodes.rationale: Displacement capacity from nonlinear static (pushover) procedure; demand from linear modal, nonlinear static, or nonlinear dynamic; Coefficient Method and Substitute Structure Method for demand.

nodes.label: 3104F.3 New MOTs
nodes.rationale: New MOTs comply with high spill classification seismic performance criteria; requires site-specific PSHA and new borings.

nodes.label: 3104F.5 Nonstructural Components and Nonbuilding Structures
nodes.rationale: Requires Level 2 seismic assessment for nonstructural components, including critical systems (fire protection, ESD, electrical power).

nodes.label: 3105F Mooring and Berthing Analysis and Design
nodes.rationale: Establishes minimum standards for safe mooring and berthing; requires mooring analysis per OCIMF MEG3 or UFC 4-159-03; Terminal Operating Limits (TOLs) based on mooring analyses.
nodes.norm_label: 3105f mooring and berthing analysis and design

nodes.label: 3105F.2 Mooring Analyses
nodes.rationale: Requires manual or numerical mooring analysis per OCIMF MEG3 or UFC 4-159-03; minimum 9 environmental and loading considerations including two current directions, tide levels, vessel conditions.

nodes.label: 3105F.3 Wave, Passing Vessel, Seiche and Tsunami
nodes.rationale: Defines criteria for when passing vessel analysis is required (>25,000 DWT, L<=500 ft, speed above critical); seiche analysis required for harbor basins; tsunami run-up assessment.
nodes.norm_label: 3105f.3 wave, passing vessel, seiche and tsunami

nodes.label: 3105F.8 Mooring Hardware
nodes.rationale: Requires bollards, quick release hooks, fittings marked with safe working loads; minimum 3 quick release hooks for tankers >= 50,000 DWT; safety factor 1.2 on MBL.

nodes.label: 3106F Geotechnical Hazards and Foundations
nodes.rationale: Provides minimum standards for geotechnical hazard analyses under static and seismic conditions; site characterization, liquefaction, slope stability, earth pressures, pile behavior.

nodes.label: 3106F.2.1 Site Classes
nodes.rationale: Defines Site Classes A through F based on shear wave velocity, SPT blow count, and undrained shear strength; Site Class F requires site-specific PSHA.

nodes.label: 3106F.4 Liquefaction Potential
nodes.rationale: Requires evaluation per NCEER, SCEC, CGS SP 117A; identifies liquefiable strata and associated hazards including lateral spreading and post-liquefaction settlement.

nodes.label: 3106F.5 Slope or Embankment Stability and Seismically Induced Lateral Spreading
nodes.rationale: Static factor of safety >= 1.5; pseudo-static seismic analysis with yield acceleration; post-earthquake factor >= 1.1; Newmark sliding block method for lateral spread.
nodes.norm_label: 3106f.5 slope or embankment stability and seismically induced lateral spreading

nodes.label: 3107F Structural Analysis and Design of Components
nodes.rationale: Establishes performance standards for concrete, steel and timber structural components; prescribes material strength factors for seismic and non-seismic conditions.

nodes.label: 3108F Fire Prevention, Detection and Suppression
nodes.rationale: Requires fire protection assessment, ESD systems, fire detection, alarms, and suppression provisions based on fire hazard classification (Low/Medium/High) and cargo volatility.

nodes.label: 3108F.3 Emergency Shutdown Systems
nodes.rationale: ESD systems per 2 CCR 2380 and 33 CFR 154.550; requires multiple actuation stations, redundancy, SIV closure synchronization, secondary power.

nodes.label: 3109F Piping and Pipelines
nodes.rationale: Minimum engineering requirements for oil piping/pipelines; pipeline stress analysis considering seismic displacements from structural analysis.

nodes.label: 3110F Mechanical Equipment
nodes.rationale: Standards for marine loading arms, winches, cranes, vapor control, sumps, and personnel access systems.

nodes.label: 3111F Electrical Systems
nodes.rationale: Requirements for electrical equipment, cathodic protection systems maintenance and testing per Section 3111F.10.

nodes.label: 3112F LNG Marine Terminals
nodes.rationale: Specific requirements for marine terminals that transfer liquefied natural gas (LNG); uses SI units; seismic return periods of 72 and 475 years.

nodes.label: 2301 General (Wood)
nodes.rationale: Establishes scope: governs materials, design, construction and quality of wood members and their fasteners. California amendments apply for DSA-SS, DSA-SS/CC, OSHPD 1, 1R, 2, 4, 5.

nodes.label: 2301.1.4 Prohibition (DSA/OSHPD)
nodes.rationale: DSA and OSHPD prohibit: straight-sheathed horizontal lumber diaphragms; gypsum-based and portland cement plaster shear walls; WSP shear walls/diaphragms with staples; unblocked shear walls; WSP sheathing not applied directly to framing; single/double diagonal lumber walls; log structures per ICC 400; CLT in seismic force-resisting system unless alternative approved.

nodes.label: 2302 Design Requirements
nodes.rationale: Enumerates five permitted design methods: ASD (Secs 2304/2305/2306), LRFD (Secs 2304/2305/2307), conventional light-frame (Secs 2304/2308), AWC WFCM (Sec 2309), and log structures per ICC 400.

nodes.label: 2303 Minimum Standards and Quality
nodes.rationale: Lists conformance requirements for all major wood product types: sawn lumber, I-joists, glulam, CLT, wood structural panels, fiberboard, hardboard, particleboard, preservative-treated wood, structural composite lumber, log members, poles/piles, fire-retardant-treated wood, hardwood plywood, trusses, joist hangers, nails, and staples.

nodes.label: 2303.1.1 Sawn Lumber
nodes.rationale: Sawn lumber for load-supporting purposes shall be identified by grade mark of a grading agency approved under DOC PS 20 or equivalent.

nodes.label: 2303.1.3 Structural Glued-Laminated Timber
nodes.rationale: Must be manufactured and identified per ANSI/APA 190.1 and ASTM D3737. DSA/OSHPD require construction documents to specify dry/wet service, laminating combinations, species group, preservative treatment, and provisions for field handling per AITC 111. Fastener/connection design must comply with AITC 117 and NDS Appendix E.

nodes.label: 2303.1.5 Wood Structural Panels
nodes.rationale: Must conform to DOC PS 1, DOC PS 2 or ANSI/APA PRP 210. Performance Category value used as nominal panel thickness.

nodes.label: 2303.2 Fire-Retardant-Treated Wood
nodes.rationale: Requires flame spread index ≤25 per ASTM E84 or UL 723 over a 20-minute test period with flame front not exceeding 10.5 ft beyond burner centerline. Chemical pressure impregnation at ≥50 psig in closed vessels.

nodes.label: 2303.4 Trusses
nodes.rationale: Covers design (2303.4.1), truss placement diagram (2303.4.2), submittal package (2303.4.3), anchorage (2303.4.4), alterations (2303.4.5), TPI 1 specifications (2303.4.6), and quality assurance (2303.4.7).

nodes.label: 2303.4.1 Truss Design and Drawings
nodes.rationale: Truss design drawings must include slope, span, spacing, joint locations, bearing widths, design loads, lateral loads, connection details, member sizes/grades, and deflection ratios. Must be submitted to building official prior to installation.

nodes.label: 2303.4.1.2 Permanent Individual Truss Member Restraint (PITMR) and Diagonal Bracing (PITMDB)
nodes.rationale: Three methods: (1) standard industry lateral restraint per TPI 1 Section 2.3.3.1.1 or Figures 2303.4.1.2(1)(3)(5); (2) individual member buckling reinforcement; (3) project-specific design by registered design professional.
nodes.norm_label: 2303.4.1.2 permanent individual truss member restraint (pitmr) and diagonal bracing (pitmdb)

nodes.label: 2303.4.1.3 Trusses Spanning 60 Feet or Greater
nodes.rationale: Owner must contract with a qualified registered design professional for temporary installation restraint/bracing and PITMR/PITMDB design.

nodes.label: 2303.6 Nails and Staples
nodes.rationale: Nails and staples must conform to ASTM F1667 including Supplement 1. Specifies minimum bending yield strengths by shank diameter range.

nodes.label: 2304.10 Connectors and Fasteners
nodes.rationale: Requirements covering fire-resistance (2304.10.1), fastener requirements/schedule (2304.10.2), sheathing fasteners (2304.10.3), joist hangers (2304.10.4), other fasteners (2304.10.5), fasteners in treated wood (2304.10.6), load path (2304.10.7), and framing requirements (2304.10.8).

nodes.label: 2304.10.6 Fasteners in Contact with Preservative-Treated and Fire-Retardant-Treated Wood
nodes.rationale: Hot-dipped zinc-coated galvanized steel, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper required for preservative-treated wood. Zinc coating weights per ASTM A153; mechanically deposited zinc coating per ASTM B695 Class 55 min.
nodes.norm_label: 2304.10.6 fasteners in contact with preservative-treated and fire-retardant-treated wood

nodes.label: 2304.11 Heavy Timber Construction
nodes.rationale: Minimum dimensions in Table 2304.11. Covers columns, floor framing, roof framing, partitions/walls, floors, and roof decks. CLT and glued-laminated options specified.

nodes.label: 2304.12 Protection Against Decay and Termites
nodes.rationale: Wood in specified locations must use naturally durable or preservative-treated wood. Locations include: joists/girders/subfloor in crawl spaces, exterior foundation walls, below-grade framing, sleepers on slabs, wood siding near grade, girder ends in masonry, posts/columns, moisture-permeable floors/roofs supports, and retaining walls. AWPA U1 is the governing standard.

nodes.label: 2304.13 Long-Term Loading
nodes.rationale: Wood members supporting concrete, masonry or similar materials must be checked for long-term loading per ANSI/AWC NDS.

nodes.label: 2305 General Design Requirements for Lateral Force-Resisting Systems
nodes.rationale: Wood-frame shear walls and diaphragms resisting wind/seismic/lateral loads must be designed per AWC SDPWS. Includes diaphragm deflection equations (Eq 23-1) and shear wall deflection (Eq 23-2).
nodes.norm_label: 2305 general design requirements for lateral force-resisting systems

nodes.label: 2305.2 Diaphragm Deflection
nodes.rationale: Deflection of blocked wood structural panel diaphragms uniformly fastened with staples calculated per Equation 23-1.

nodes.label: 2305.3 Shear Wall Deflection
nodes.rationale: Deflection of blocked wood structural panel shear walls uniformly fastened with staples per Equation 23-2.

nodes.label: 2306 Allowable Stress Design
nodes.rationale: ASD design must follow Table 2306.1 standards list (AWC NDS, SDPWS, ASABE EP 484.3/486.3/559.1, APA standards, AITC standards, TPI 1, etc.). Addresses joists/rafters, plank/beam flooring, treated wood stress adjustments, lumber decking, diaphragms and shear walls.

nodes.label: 2306.2 Wood-Frame Diaphragms
nodes.rationale: Design per AWC SDPWS. Allowable shear values for staple-fastened panels in Tables 2306.2(1) and 2306.2(2). Values may be increased 40% for wind design.

nodes.label: 2306.3 Wood-Frame Shear Walls
nodes.rationale: Design per AWC SDPWS. Allowable shear values in Tables 2306.3(1), 2306.3(2), 2306.3(3). Values may be increased 40% for wind design.

nodes.label: 2307 Load and Resistance Factor Design
nodes.rationale: LRFD design per ANSI/AWC NDS and AWC SDPWS.

nodes.label: 2308 Conventional Light-Frame Construction
nodes.rationale: Prescriptive requirements for light-frame construction with limitations: stories per SDC (Table 2308.2.1), floor-to-floor height ≤11 ft 7 in, dead load ≤15 psf, live load ≤40 psf, ground snow load ≤50 psf, basic wind speed V ≤130 mph. Not permitted for Risk Category IV in SDC B-F.

nodes.label: 2308.3 Foundations and Footings
nodes.rationale: Foundation plates must be bolted with min 1/2-in diameter bolts embedded min 7 in into concrete/masonry, max 6 ft on center. SDC D requires steel plate washers 0.229 in x 3 in x 3 in. SDC E requires 5/8-in diameter bolts.

nodes.label: 2308.4 Floor Framing

nodes.label: 1001.1 General Administration
nodes.rationale: Establishes that buildings shall be provided with a means of egress system as required by Chapter 10, controlling design, construction, and arrangement of egress components.

nodes.label: 1002.1 Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Requires means of egress to be maintained in accordance with the California Fire Code.

nodes.label: 1003.1 Applicability - General Means of Egress
nodes.rationale: Sections 1003-1015 apply to all three elements of the means of egress: exit access, exit, and exit discharge.

nodes.label: 1003.2 Ceiling Height
nodes.rationale: Minimum ceiling height of 7 ft 6 in (2286 mm) above finished floor; Group I-2, I-2.1, I-3 require 8 ft (2439 mm).

nodes.label: 1003.3 Protruding Objects
nodes.rationale: Protruding objects on circulation paths must meet headroom, post-mounted, horizontal projection, and clear width requirements.

nodes.label: 1003.6 Means of Egress Continuity
nodes.rationale: Path of egress travel shall not be interrupted by non-egress building elements; minimum width shall not be diminished along path of travel.

nodes.label: 1004.1 Design Occupant Load
nodes.rationale: Number of occupants for whom egress facilities are provided shall be determined per Section 1004.

nodes.label: 1004.5 Areas Without Fixed Seating
nodes.rationale: Occupant load computed at one occupant per unit of area per Table 1004.5; not less than calculated value.

nodes.label: 1004.6 Fixed Seating
nodes.rationale: Occupant load for fixed seating areas based on number of fixed seats installed; booths at 1 per 24-inch length.

nodes.label: 1004.9 Posting of Occupant Load
nodes.rationale: Assembly, classroom, dining spaces with OL >= 50 must post occupant load conspicuously near main exit.

nodes.label: 1005.1 General Means of Egress Sizing
nodes.rationale: All portions of the means of egress system shall be sized in accordance with Section 1005.

nodes.label: 1005.3 Required Capacity Based on Occupant Load
nodes.rationale: Egress capacity in inches = occupant load x capacity factor; stairways: 0.3 in/occupant (or 0.2 in sprinklered); other components: 0.2 in/occupant (or 0.15 in sprinklered).
nodes.norm_label: 1005.3 required capacity based on occupant load

nodes.label: 1005.5 Distribution of Minimum Width and Required Capacity
nodes.rationale: Loss of any one exit shall not reduce available capacity or width to less than 50% of required.
nodes.norm_label: 1005.5 distribution of minimum width and required capacity

nodes.label: 1006.1 General - Number of Exits
nodes.rationale: Number of exits or exit access doorways shall comply with Section 1006.2 for spaces and Section 1006.3 for stories.

nodes.label: 1006.2.1 Egress Based on Occupant Load and Common Path
nodes.rationale: Two exits required where occupant load or common path of egress travel exceeds values in Table 1006.2.1.
nodes.norm_label: 1006.2.1 egress based on occupant load and common path

nodes.label: 1006.3.3 Egress Based on Occupant Load per Story
nodes.rationale: Minimum number of exits per story based on occupant load per Table 1006.3.3.
nodes.norm_label: 1006.3.3 egress based on occupant load per story

nodes.label: 1006.3.4 Single Exits
nodes.rationale: Single exit or access to single exit is permitted under specified conditions including occupant load and travel distance limits in Tables 1006.3.4(1) and 1006.3.4(2).

nodes.label: 1007.1.1 Two Exits Separation
nodes.rationale: Where two exits are required, they shall be separated by at least one-half the diagonal dimension of the building or area served.

nodes.label: 1008.1 Means of Egress Illumination
nodes.rationale: Illumination required in means of egress at all times room is occupied; emergency power required for 90 minutes upon failure.

nodes.label: 1008.2.1 Illumination Level Under Normal Power
nodes.rationale: Minimum 1 footcandle at walking surface; 10 footcandles at stairways when in use.

nodes.label: 1009.1 Accessible Means of Egress Required
nodes.rationale: Accessible spaces shall be provided with not less than one accessible means of egress; number matches required exits per Section 1006.

nodes.label: 1009.3 Accessible Means of Egress Stairways
nodes.rationale: Stairways used as accessible means of egress must have 48-inch clear width between handrails (exceptions apply for sprinklered buildings).

nodes.label: 1009.4 Accessible Means of Egress Elevators
nodes.rationale: Elevators used as accessible means of egress must have standby power and area of refuge access.

nodes.label: 1009.6 Areas of Refuge
nodes.rationale: Areas of refuge must be accessible from the space served, sized with 30x52 inch wheelchair spaces, separated by smoke barrier, and equipped with two-way communication.

nodes.label: 1010.1 General - Doors in Means of Egress
nodes.rationale: Doors in means of egress must comply with sections 1010.1.1 through 1010.3.4; must be readily distinguishable from adjacent construction.
nodes.norm_label: 1010.1 general - doors in means of egress

nodes.label: 1010.1.1 Size of Doors
nodes.rationale: Minimum clear opening width 32 inches; height 80 inches; Group I-2 bed/stretcher doors require 44-inch clear width.

nodes.label: 1010.2 Door Operations
nodes.rationale: Egress doors shall be readily openable from the egress side without key or special knowledge; unlatching requires not more than one motion.

nodes.label: 1010.2.9 Panic and Fire Exit Hardware
nodes.rationale: Panic hardware required for Group H and rooms with OL 50+ in Group A or E; listed per UL 305 (panic) or UL 10C and UL 305 (fire exit).

nodes.label: 1010.2.13 Delayed Egress
nodes.rationale: Delayed egress locking systems permitted in Groups B, F, I, M, R, S, U in fully sprinklered buildings with smoke detection; max 15-second delay (30 seconds for Alzheimer's facilities).

nodes.label: 1011.1 General - Stairways
nodes.rationale: Stairways serving occupied portions of a building shall comply with Sections 1011.2 through 1011.13.

nodes.label: 1011.2 Stairway Width and Capacity
nodes.rationale: Required capacity per Section 1005.1; minimum 44 inches (36 inches for OL < 50).

nodes.label: 1011.5.2 Riser Height and Tread Depth
nodes.rationale: Riser heights max 7 inches, min 4 inches; tread depth min 11 inches.

nodes.label: 1011.6 Stairway Landings
nodes.rationale: Floor or landing required at top and bottom of each stairway; width >= stairway width; depth >= width or 48 inches (whichever is less).

nodes.label: 1011.11 Handrails on Stairways
nodes.rationale: Flights of stairways shall have handrails on each side complying with Section 1014.

nodes.label: 1012.1 Scope - Ramps
nodes.rationale: Provisions apply to ramps used as a component of a means of egress.

nodes.label: 1012.2 Ramp Slope
nodes.rationale: Egress ramps max slope 1:12 (8.3%); other pedestrian ramps max 1:8 (12.5%).

nodes.label: 1013.1 Exit Signs - Where Required
nodes.rationale: Exits and exit access doors shall be marked by approved exit signs visible from any direction of egress travel.

nodes.label: 1013.5 Internally Illuminated Exit Signs
nodes.rationale: Exit signs listed and labeled per UL 924; illuminated at all times.

nodes.label: 1014.1 Handrails - Where Required
nodes.rationale: Handrails required on stairways per Section 1011.11, ramps per Section 1012.8, and stepped/ramped aisles per Section 1030.16.

nodes.label: 1014.2 Handrail Height
nodes.rationale: Handrail height 34-38 inches above stair tread nosings or ramp surface; alternating tread devices 30-34 inches.

nodes.label: 1015.1 General - Guards
nodes.rationale: Guards required along open-sided walking surfaces more than 30 inches above floor or grade below.

nodes.label: 1015.3 Guard Height
nodes.rationale: Required guards shall be not less than 42 inches high; exceptions for R-2/R-3 stair sides (34 inches) and assembly seating areas.

nodes.label: 1016.1 General - Exit Access
nodes.rationale: Exit access shall comply with Sections 1003-1015; exit access arrangement shall comply with Sections 1016-1021.

nodes.label: 1017.1 General - Exit Access Travel Distance
nodes.rationale: Travel distance within exit access shall not exceed values in Table 1017.2; measured from most remote point along natural and unobstructed path to exit.

nodes.label: 1020.1 General - Corridors
nodes.rationale: Corridors serving as exit access component must comply with Sections 1020.2-1020.7 including fire-resistance ratings per Table 1020.2.

nodes.label: 1020.5 Dead Ends
nodes.rationale: Dead-end corridors shall not exceed 20 feet where more than one exit is required; exceptions up to 50 feet in certain occupancies with sprinklers.

nodes.label: 1022.1 General - Exits
nodes.rationale: Exits shall comply with Sections 1022-1027; level of exit protection shall not be reduced until arrival at exit discharge.

nodes.label: 1023.1 General - Interior Exit Stairways and Ramps
nodes.rationale: Interior exit stairways and ramps shall be enclosed, lead to exterior, and not be used for any purpose other than means of egress.
nodes.norm_label: 1023.1 general - interior exit stairways and ramps

nodes.label: 1023.2 Interior Exit Stairway Construction
nodes.rationale: Enclosures shall be fire barriers per Section 707 or horizontal assemblies per Section 711; 2-hour rating connecting 4+ stories, 1-hour for fewer.

nodes.label: 1024.1 General - Exit Passageways
nodes.rationale: Exit passageways shall not be used for any purpose other than means of egress and circulation path.

nodes.label: 1025.1 General - Luminous Egress Path Markings
nodes.rationale: Luminous egress path markings required in high-rise buildings of Groups A, B, E, M, or R-1.

nodes.label: 1026.1 General - Horizontal Exits
nodes.rationale: Horizontal exits shall not be the only exit from a building portion; not more than 50% of exits (exceptions for I-2 and I-3 occupancies).

nodes.label: 1027.1 General - Exterior Exit Stairways and Ramps
nodes.rationale: Exterior exit stairways and ramps shall not be used for Group I-2; permitted for buildings not exceeding six stories above grade plane.
nodes.norm_label: 1027.1 general - exterior exit stairways and ramps

nodes.label: 1028.1 General - Exit Discharge
nodes.rationale: Exit discharge shall comply with Sections 1028-1029 and applicable requirements of Sections 1003-1015.

nodes.label: 1028.2 Exit Discharge Requirements
nodes.rationale: Exits shall discharge directly to exterior; exit discharge shall be at grade or provide direct path to grade; shall not re-enter building.

nodes.label: 1029.1 General - Egress Courts
nodes.rationale: Egress courts serving as exit discharge components shall comply with this section; minimum 44 inches width.

nodes.label: 1030.1 General - Assembly Egress
nodes.rationale: Rooms or spaces used for assembly with seats, tables, displays shall comply with Section 1030 including special aisle capacity factors.

nodes.label: 1030.2 Assembly Main Exit
nodes.rationale: Main exit of assembly with OL > 300 must accommodate not less than one-half the occupant load and front on street or 20-foot unoccupied space.

nodes.label: 1030.6.2 Smoke-Protected Assembly Seating Capacity
nodes.rationale: Reduced aisle capacity factors permitted for smoke-protected assembly seating per Table 1030.6.2; life safety evaluation per NFPA 101 required.

nodes.label: 1030.8 Common Path of Egress Travel - Assembly
nodes.rationale: Common path of egress travel shall not exceed 30 feet from any seat to a choice of two paths; 75 feet for < 50 occupants; 50 feet for smoke-protected or open-air.
nodes.norm_label: 1030.8 common path of egress travel - assembly

nodes.label: Table 1004.5 Maximum Floor Area Allowances Per Occupant
nodes.rationale: Provides occupant load factors (sq ft per occupant) for various occupancy functions including assembly, business, educational, institutional, and mercantile spaces.
nodes.norm_label: table 1004.5 maximum floor area allowances per occupant

nodes.label: Table 1006.2.1 Spaces With One Exit or Exit Access Doorway
nodes.rationale: Maximum occupant load and common path of egress travel distance by occupancy for spaces allowed a single exit; includes sprinklered and non-sprinklered conditions.
nodes.norm_label: table 1006.2.1 spaces with one exit or exit access doorway

nodes.label: Table 1006.3.3 Minimum Number of Exits Per Story
nodes.rationale: Requires 2 exits for OL 1-500, 3 exits for OL 501-1000, 4 exits for OL > 1000 per story.
nodes.norm_label: table 1006.3.3 minimum number of exits per story

nodes.label: Table 1006.3.4(1) Stories With One Exit for R-2 and R-3
nodes.rationale: Maximum dwelling units and travel distance per story for single exit in R-2 and R-3 occupancies.
nodes.norm_label: table 1006.3.4(1) stories with one exit for r-2 and r-3

nodes.label: Table 1006.3.4(2) Stories With One Exit for Other Occupancies
nodes.rationale: Maximum occupant load and travel distance per story for single exit in non-R-2/R-3 occupancies.
nodes.norm_label: table 1006.3.4(2) stories with one exit for other occupancies

nodes.label: Table 1017.2 Exit Access Travel Distance
nodes.rationale: Maximum exit access travel distances by occupancy with and without sprinkler systems.

nodes.label: Table 1020.2 Corridor Fire-Resistance Rating
nodes.rationale: Required corridor fire-resistance ratings by occupancy and occupant load, with and without sprinkler systems.

nodes.label: Table 1020.3 Minimum Corridor Width
nodes.rationale: Minimum corridor widths by occupancy type; Group I-2 bed movement areas require 96 inches.

nodes.label: Table 1030.6.2 Capacity for Aisles for Smoke-Protected Assembly
nodes.rationale: Inches of capacity per seat served for smoke-protected assembly seating areas, varying by total number of seats and aisle type.
nodes.norm_label: table 1030.6.2 capacity for aisles for smoke-protected assembly

nodes.label: Defined Term: Means of Egress
nodes.rationale: A continuous and unobstructed path of vertical and horizontal egress travel from any occupied portion of a building to a public way; consists of three parts: exit access, exit, and exit discharge.

nodes.label: Defined Term: Exit Access
nodes.rationale: The portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building to an exit.

nodes.label: Defined Term: Exit
nodes.rationale: The portion of a means of egress system between the exit access and the exit discharge; exit types include interior stairways, exterior stairways, ramps, horizontal exits, and exit passageways.

nodes.label: Defined Term: Exit Discharge
nodes.rationale: The portion of a means of egress system between the termination of an exit and a public way.

nodes.label: Defined Term: Occupant Load
nodes.rationale: The number of persons for which the means of egress of a building or portion thereof is designed; determined per Section 1004 and Table 1004.5.

nodes.label: Defined Term: Common Path of Egress Travel
nodes.rationale: That portion of the exit access travel distance measured from the most remote point within a space to that point where the occupants have separate and distinct access to two exits or exit access doorways.
nodes.norm_label: defined term: common path of egress travel

nodes.label: Defined Term: Exit Access Travel Distance
nodes.rationale: Measured from the most remote point of each room, area, or space along the natural and unobstructed path of egress travel to the entrance to an exit.
nodes.norm_label: defined term: exit access travel distance

nodes.label: Defined Term: Area of Refuge
nodes.rationale: An area where persons unable to use stairways can remain temporarily to await instructions or assistance during emergency evacuation.

nodes.label: Concept: Egress Capacity
nodes.rationale: The number of persons an egress component can accommodate; calculated by dividing component width by capacity factor (inches per occupant).
