nodes.norm_label: standard: astm e2072 - photoluminescent safety markings

nodes.label: Concept: Egress Width
nodes.rationale: The clear width of egress components; minimum based on component type and reduced capacity factors available for sprinklered buildings.

nodes.label: Concept: Smoke-Protected Assembly Seating
nodes.rationale: Assembly seating areas provided with smoke control and meeting roof height requirements; allows reduced aisle capacity factors per Table 1030.6.2.

nodes.label: 901.1 Scope
nodes.rationale: Specifies where fire protection and life safety systems are required and applies to their design, installation, and operation.

nodes.label: 901.6 Supervisory Service
nodes.rationale: Fire protection systems shall be monitored by an approved supervising station in accordance with NFPA 72.

nodes.label: 901.6.1 Automatic Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: Automatic sprinkler systems shall be monitored by an approved supervising station; exceptions for one- and two-family dwellings and limited area systems.

nodes.label: 901.6.2 Integrated Testing
nodes.rationale: Where two or more fire protection systems are interconnected, integrated testing shall be performed in accordance with NFPA 4 prior to certificate of occupancy and at intervals not exceeding 10 years.

nodes.label: 903.2 Where Required — Automatic Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: Approved automatic sprinkler systems in new buildings shall be provided in locations described in Sections 903.2.1 through 903.2.21.

nodes.label: 903.2.1.1 Group A-1
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required when fire area exceeds 12,000 sq ft, occupant load 300+, floor other than exit discharge, or contains multitheater complex.

nodes.label: 903.2.1.2 Group A-2
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required when fire area exceeds 5,000 sq ft, occupant load 100+, or structure exceeds 5,000 sq ft with multiple fire areas.

nodes.label: 903.2.1.3 Group A-3
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required when fire area exceeds 12,000 sq ft, occupant load 300+, or structure exceeds 12,000 sq ft with multiple fire areas containing exhibition/display rooms.

nodes.label: 903.2.1.5 Group A-5
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required for all enclosed Group A-5 accessory use areas exceeding 1,000 sq ft.

nodes.label: 903.2.2 Ambulatory Care Facilities
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required when 4 or more care recipients are incapable of self-preservation or when such recipients are above exit discharge level.

nodes.label: 903.2.5.2 Group H-5 Occupancies
nodes.rationale: Design shall meet occupancy hazard classifications per Table 903.2.5.2.

nodes.label: Table 903.2.5.2 Group H-5 Sprinkler Design Criteria
nodes.rationale: Lists occupancy hazard classifications (Ordinary Group 2, Extra Hazard Group 2) for different locations within H-5 occupancies.
nodes.norm_label: table 903.2.5.2 group h-5 sprinkler design criteria

nodes.label: 903.2.6.2 Group I-3
nodes.rationale: Every building housing inmates shall be protected by an automatic sprinkler system conforming to NFPA 13 with electrically supervised control valves.

nodes.label: 903.2.8 Group R
nodes.rationale: Automatic sprinkler system required throughout all buildings with a Group R fire area.

nodes.label: 903.2.11.1 Stories Without Openings
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required when floor area exceeds 1,500 sq ft and story does not meet exterior wall opening criteria.

nodes.label: 903.2.11.3 Buildings 55 Feet or More in Height
nodes.rationale: Sprinkler required throughout buildings with one or more stories with occupant load of 30+ located 55 feet or more above lowest fire department vehicle access.
nodes.norm_label: 903.2.11.3 buildings 55 feet or more in height

nodes.label: 903.3.1.1 NFPA 13 Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: Default standard for full sprinkler protection; installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13 as amended in Chapter 35.

nodes.label: 903.3.1.2 NFPA 13R Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: Permitted in Group R occupancies of 4 stories or fewer above grade plane and floor level of highest story 30 feet or less above lowest fire department vehicle access.

nodes.label: 903.3.1.3 NFPA 13D Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: Permitted in one- and two-family dwellings, Group R-3, R-4 Condition 1, and townhouses.

nodes.label: 903.3.2 Quick-Response and Residential Sprinklers
nodes.rationale: Quick-response or residential sprinklers required in smoke compartments with care recipient sleeping units in Group I-2, gas fireplace areas in Group I-2, treatment rooms in ambulatory care facilities, Group R dwelling/sleeping units, and light-hazard occupancies per NFPA 13.

nodes.label: 903.4 Sprinkler System Supervision and Alarms
nodes.rationale: All valves controlling water supply, pumps, tanks, waterflow switches shall be electrically supervised by a listed fire alarm control unit.

nodes.label: 904.13 Commercial Cooking Systems
nodes.rationale: Commercial cooking equipment producing grease-laden vapors requires Type I Hood and automatic fire extinguishing system listed for intended use.

nodes.label: 905.2 Installation Standard — Standpipes
nodes.rationale: Standpipe systems shall be installed in accordance with this section and NFPA 14.

nodes.label: 905.3.1 Height — Standpipe
nodes.rationale: Class III standpipes required when highest story is more than 30 feet above lowest fire department vehicle access, or building is four or more stories in height.

nodes.label: Section 907 Fire Alarm and Detection Systems
nodes.norm_label: section 907 fire alarm and detection systems

nodes.label: 907.2 Where Required — Fire Alarm Systems
nodes.rationale: Fire alarm system required in new buildings in accordance with Sections 907.2.1 through 907.2.29 and in accordance with NFPA 72.

nodes.label: 907.2.1 Group A — Fire Alarm
nodes.rationale: Manual fire alarm required when occupant load is 300+ or more than 100 persons above/below exit discharge.

nodes.label: 907.2.2 Group B — Fire Alarm
nodes.rationale: Manual fire alarm required when combined Group B occupant load is 500+ or 100+ above/below exit discharge or fire area contains ambulatory care facility.

nodes.label: 907.2.3 Group E — Fire Alarm
nodes.rationale: Manual and automatic fire alarm system with emergency voice/alarm communication required for Group E with 50+ occupants or more than one classroom.

nodes.label: 907.2.11 Single- and Multiple-Station Smoke Alarms
nodes.rationale: Listed single- and multiple-station smoke alarms complying with UL 217 required.

nodes.label: 907.2.13 High-Rise Buildings and Group I-2 — Fire Alarm
nodes.rationale: Buildings with occupied floors 75 feet above lowest fire department vehicle access require automatic smoke detection, fire department communication system, and emergency voice/alarm communication system.
nodes.norm_label: 907.2.13 high-rise buildings and group i-2 — fire alarm

nodes.label: 907.5.2.2 Emergency Voice/Alarm Communication Systems
nodes.rationale: Required systems shall be designed and installed in accordance with NFPA 72.

nodes.label: 907.6.6 Monitoring — Fire Alarm Systems
nodes.rationale: Fire alarm systems required by this chapter shall be monitored by an approved supervising station in accordance with NFPA 72.

nodes.label: Section 909 Smoke Control Systems
nodes.rationale: Applies to mechanical or passive smoke control systems to provide tenable environment for evacuation.

nodes.label: 909.6 Pressurization Method
nodes.rationale: Primary mechanical means of controlling smoke shall be by pressure differences across smoke barriers; minimum 0.05-inch water gage in fully sprinklered buildings.

nodes.label: 909.7 Airflow Design Method
nodes.rationale: Airflow method permitted when approved by fire code official; designed in accordance with NFPA 92.

nodes.label: 909.8 Exhaust Method
nodes.rationale: Mechanical smoke control for large enclosed volumes (atriums, malls) using exhaust method designed in accordance with NFPA 92.

nodes.label: 909.21 Elevator Hoistway Pressurization Alternative
nodes.rationale: Elevator hoistway pressurization provided in lieu of enclosed elevator lobbies; minimum 0.10 inch water positive pressure.

nodes.label: 910.2.1 Group F-1 or S-1 — Smoke and Heat Removal
nodes.rationale: Required in buildings used as Group F-1 or S-1 with more than 50,000 sq ft of undivided area.
nodes.norm_label: 910.2.1 group f-1 or s-1 — smoke and heat removal

nodes.label: Section 911 Fire Command Center
nodes.rationale: Required in high-rise buildings, F-1 and S-1 occupancies with footprint over 500,000 sq ft, and Group I-2 with occupied floors more than 75 feet above lowest fire department vehicle access.

nodes.label: 911.1.6 Required Features — Fire Command Center
nodes.rationale: Lists 19 required features including emergency voice/alarm communication system, fire department communications, sprinkler valve panels, standby power status, etc.

nodes.label: Section 915 Carbon Monoxide Detection
nodes.rationale: Required in Group I-2, I-4 and R occupancies and classrooms in Group E where fuel-burning appliances, fuel-burning fireplaces, fuel-burning forced-air furnaces, or attached private garages exist.

nodes.label: 1101A Application
nodes.rationale: Establishes scope of Chapter 11A: newly-constructed covered multifamily dwellings, new common use areas, additions, and interior gut-rehabs. Excludes public accommodations (hotels/motels) subject to Ch 11B.

nodes.label: 1102A.1 Where Required
nodes.rationale: Each building on a site evaluated separately except when calculating number of units required to comply under 1102A.3.1. Units in same structure separated by firewalls are not separate buildings.

nodes.label: 1102A.2 Existing Buildings
nodes.rationale: Chapter 11A does not apply to alterations/repairs to multifamily dwellings first occupied on or before March 13, 1991. Buildings must be maintained to accessibility standards in effect at time of construction.

nodes.label: 1102A.3.1 Multistory Apartment/Condo in Buildings Without Elevator
nodes.rationale: Applies to permits on/after July 1, 2005; at least 10% but not less than 1 of multistory dwellings in apt buildings (3+ units) or condos (4+ units) shall comply with accessible entry, powder room/bathroom on entry level, and all rooms on entry level on accessible route.
nodes.norm_label: 1102a.3.1 multistory apartment/condo in buildings without elevator

nodes.label: 1102A.3.2 Multistory Dwelling Units in Buildings With One or More Elevators
nodes.rationale: Elevator-served floor treated as ground floor; primary entry floor must have at least one powder room/bathroom, at least one kitchen, and all rooms on entry level on accessible route.
nodes.norm_label: 1102a.3.2 multistory dwelling units in buildings with one or more elevators

nodes.label: 1102A.4 Temporary Restrictions
nodes.rationale: During partial/restricted use, primary entrances shall remain accessible to persons with disabilities.

nodes.label: 1104A Covered Multifamily Dwellings
nodes.rationale: All ground-floor units in non-elevator buildings shall be adaptable and on an accessible route unless site impracticality (1150A) applies.

nodes.label: 1105A Garages, Carports and Parking Facilities
nodes.rationale: Garages, carports and other parking facilities accessory to covered multifamily dwelling units shall be accessible per Section 1109A.

nodes.label: 1106A Site and Building Characteristics
nodes.rationale: Elevator buildings must provide at least one accessible entrance regardless of terrain. Non-elevator buildings must provide accessible entrance unless terrain prevents it per site impracticality tests.

nodes.label: 1107A Definitions
nodes.rationale: All definitions located in Chapter 2 of the CBC.

nodes.label: 1108A General Requirements for Accessible Parking and Exterior Routes of Travel
nodes.norm_label: 1108a general requirements for accessible parking and exterior routes of travel

nodes.label: 1109A.2.1 Private Garages
nodes.rationale: Private garages accessory to covered multifamily units must be accessible. Exception for single-unit attached garage if direct door or accessible route is provided.

nodes.label: 1109A.3 Required Accessible Parking Spaces
nodes.rationale: Minimum 2% of covered multifamily dwelling units; at least one space of each parking type shall be accessible.

nodes.label: 1109A.4 Assigned Accessible Parking Spaces
nodes.rationale: When assigned parking provided, at least 2% of assigned spaces shall be accessible per parking type.

nodes.label: 1109A.5 Unassigned and Visitor Parking Spaces
nodes.rationale: At least 5% of unassigned/visitor spaces shall be accessible and provide access to grade-level entrances.

nodes.label: 1109A.7 Location of Accessible Parking Spaces
nodes.rationale: Must be on shortest possible accessible route; dispersed near multiple accessible entrances; accessible route shall not cross vehicular lanes where practical.

nodes.label: 1109A.8 Design and Construction of Accessible Parking
nodes.norm_label: 1109a.8 design and construction of accessible parking

nodes.label: 1109A.8.1 Vertical Clearances
nodes.rationale: Minimum 8 ft 2 in (2489 mm) vertical clearance for all entrances/exits/passageways serving accessible parking.

nodes.label: 1109A.8.5 Accessible Single Parking Space
nodes.rationale: 14 ft (4267 mm) minimum width with 9-ft parking area and 5-ft access aisle; 18 ft (5486 mm) minimum length; access aisle marked with blue border and hatching.

nodes.label: 1109A.8.6 Van Accessible Parking Space
nodes.rationale: 1 in 8 accessible spaces shall be van accessible; 17 ft (5181 mm) minimum width; 18 ft minimum length; designated 'Van Accessible'.

nodes.label: 1110A Exterior Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Accessible routes must connect public transportation stops, parking, public streets to accessible building entrances. Must coincide with general public route to maximum extent feasible.

nodes.label: 1111A Changes in Level on Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Max abrupt change 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) beveled at max 1:2; changes <= 1/4 inch may be vertical; changes > 1/2 inch require sloped surface max 1:20, curb ramp, ramp, elevator, or platform lift.
nodes.norm_label: 1111a changes in level on accessible routes

nodes.label: 1112A Curb Ramps on Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Required at street intersections and pedestrian way/curb crossings; preferred at crosswalk center; minimum 48 inches wide; max slope 1:12 (8.33%).

nodes.label: 1113A Walks and Sidewalks on Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Minimum 48 inches (1219 mm) width, reducible to 36 inches (914 mm) for individual dwelling unit walks; continuous, stable, firm, slip-resistant surface; max cross slope 1:48.
nodes.norm_label: 1113a walks and sidewalks on accessible routes

nodes.label: 1114A Exterior Ramps and Landings on Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Min 48 inches wide; max slope 1:12 (8.33%); max cross slope 1:48; handrails required each side when slope > 1:20.
nodes.norm_label: 1114a exterior ramps and landings on accessible routes

nodes.label: 1115A Exterior Stairways
nodes.rationale: No open risers; stable/firm/slip-resistant treads; nosing max 1-1/4 inch projection; visual contrast striping on upper approach and all treads; handrails on each side.

nodes.label: 1116A Hazards on Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Abrupt level changes >4 inches require warning curbs; min 80-inch headroom clearance; overhanging obstructions min 80 inches above walking surface.

nodes.label: 1117A General Requirements for Accessible Entrances, Exits, Interior Routes
nodes.rationale: All primary entrances and exterior ground-floor exit doors on accessible routes shall be accessible. Ground-floor units with separate entrances each served by accessible route.
nodes.norm_label: 1117a general requirements for accessible entrances, exits, interior routes

nodes.label: 1119A Interior Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Interior accessible routes shall connect entrances to covered dwelling units and common areas; routes shall not pass through kitchens, storage, restrooms or closets. Min 44 inches for occupant load >= 10; 36 inches for < 10.

nodes.label: 1121A Changes in Level on Interior Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Mirrors exterior 1111A requirements for interior accessible routes.
nodes.norm_label: 1121a changes in level on interior accessible routes

nodes.label: 1122A Interior Ramps and Landings on Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Interior ramp requirements parallel to exterior (1114A): min 48 in wide, max 1:12 slope, handrails each side when slope > 1:20.
nodes.norm_label: 1122a interior ramps and landings on accessible routes

nodes.label: 1123A Interior Stairways
nodes.rationale: No open risers; visual contrast striping required (exception: within individual dwelling unit); handrails on each side.

nodes.label: 1124A Elevators and Platform (Wheelchair) Lifts
nodes.rationale: Elevators in covered multifamily buildings shall be accessible; must comply with ASME A17.1, Title 8 CCR Elevator Safety Orders.

nodes.label: 1124A.3 Size of Cab and Control Locations
nodes.norm_label: 1124a.3 size of cab and control locations

nodes.label: 1124A.11 Platform (Wheelchair) Lifts
nodes.rationale: Platform lifts may substitute for passenger elevators when allowed by ASME A18.1 and Title 8 CCR; must be unassisted operation; standby power required.

nodes.label: 1125A Hazards on Interior Accessible Routes
nodes.rationale: Same requirements as 1116A applied to interior: warning curbs for level changes > 4 inches, 80-inch headroom, overhanging obstruction protection.

nodes.label: 1126A Doors, Gates and Windows
nodes.rationale: Doors to common use areas or covered multifamily dwellings: min 36 in wide, 80 in high, 32 in clear opening at 90 degrees; max 8.5 lb force exterior, 5 lb interior.

nodes.label: 1126A.6 Hand-Activated Door or Gate Hardware
nodes.rationale: Lever-type, panic bars, push-pull hardware; centered 30-44 inches above floor; operable with single effort without grasping.

nodes.label: 1127A Common Use Facilities
nodes.rationale: Common use areas including lobbies, toilet/bathing facilities, laundry, community rooms, fitness facilities etc. shall be accessible.

nodes.label: 1127A.2 Toilet Facilities
nodes.rationale: At least 1% of fixtures but not less than one of each type in common use toilet facilities shall comply.

nodes.label: 1127A.2.1 Multiple-Accommodation Toilet Facilities
nodes.rationale: 60-inch turning space; accessible water closet compartment 60 in x 56/59 in; grab bars on side and rear walls; compartment door 32/34 in clear opening.

nodes.label: 1127A.2.3 Water Closets
nodes.rationale: Height 17-19 inches to top of seat; hand-operated or automatic flush controls; no spring-to-lifted seats.

nodes.label: 1127A.3 Accessible Lavatories
nodes.rationale: At least 1% of lavatories; centerline min 18 inches from wall; max rim 34 inches above floor; 30x48 inch clear floor space; knee and toe space per 1138A.2.

nodes.label: 1127A.4 Grab Bars, Tub and Shower Seats, Fasteners and Mounting Devices
nodes.rationale: Horizontal installation 33-36 inches above floor; 1-1/4 to 2 inch diameter; structural strength for 250 lb point load; 1-1/2 inch spacing from wall.
nodes.norm_label: 1127a.4 grab bars, tub and shower seats, fasteners and mounting devices

nodes.label: 1127A.5 Bathing Facilities
nodes.rationale: At least 1% of each type of bathing fixture in common use facilities; at least one of each type in each facility.

nodes.label: 1127A.5.2 Bathtubs
nodes.rationale: 48 in x 30 in minimum clear floor space; removable or permanent seat 17-19 in high; grab bars per 1127A.5.2.3; shower spray unit with 59-inch hose.

nodes.label: 1127A.5.3 Shower Compartments
nodes.rationale: Standard roll-in: 30x60 in min or 42x48 in; alternate roll-in: 36x60 in; threshold max 1/2 in; folding seat on side wall adjacent to controls.

nodes.label: 1127A.7 Signs for Toilet and Bathing Facilities
nodes.rationale: Geometric symbols: triangle (men), circle (women), circle+triangle (unisex); centered 58-60 inches AFF; ISA required.
nodes.norm_label: 1127a.7 signs for toilet and bathing facilities

nodes.label: 1127A.10 Common Accessible Laundry Rooms
nodes.rationale: At least one of each appliance type shall be accessible; front-loading washers/dryers required; controls within reach range; bottom of laundry compartment 15-36 inches AFF.

nodes.label: 1127A.12 Fixed or Built-In Seating, Tables and Counters
nodes.rationale: 5% but not less than 1 of fixed seating/tables shall be accessible; 28-34 inches height; knee and toe space.
nodes.norm_label: 1127a.12 fixed or built-in seating, tables and counters

nodes.label: 1128A Covered Dwelling Units
nodes.rationale: Covered multifamily units shall be adaptable and accessible into and throughout the unit as provided in Division IV.

nodes.label: 1130A Accessible Route Within Covered Multifamily Dwelling Units
nodes.rationale: Accessible route through all rooms and spaces; connects primary entry, additional exterior doors, kitchen appliance clear floor spaces, and bathroom fixtures. Min 36 inches wide.
nodes.norm_label: 1130a accessible route within covered multifamily dwelling units

nodes.label: 1131A Changes in Level on Interior Dwelling Unit Accessible Routes
nodes.norm_label: 1131a changes in level on interior dwelling unit accessible routes

nodes.label: 1132A.1 Primary Entry Doors and Required Exit Doors
nodes.rationale: Width and height per 1126A.1; maneuvering clearances per 1126A.3 at common/public use side.
nodes.norm_label: 1132a.1 primary entry doors and required exit doors

nodes.label: 1132A.3 Width and Height of Interior Doors and Secondary Exterior Doors
nodes.rationale: Min 6 ft 8 in (2032 mm) height; min 32 in (813 mm) clear opening at 90 degrees; capable of opening at least 90 degrees.
nodes.norm_label: 1132a.3 width and height of interior doors and secondary exterior doors

nodes.label: 1132A.4 Level Floor or Landing at Doors
nodes.rationale: Impervious exterior landings max 1/2 inch height change; pervious landings same level as interior; secondary doors to decks/patios max 4 in or 1 in with 1:8 ramp.
nodes.norm_label: 1132a.4 level floor or landing at doors

nodes.label: 1132A.5 Maneuvering Clearances at Doors
nodes.rationale: Dwelling unit side of primary entry/exit door: min 44-inch landing depth; interior doors: min 42 inches both sides (exception: 39 in when 34 in clear opening provided); strike edge 18 inches past.

nodes.label: 1132A.8 Hand-Activated Door Hardware
nodes.rationale: Lever-type hardware centered 30-44 inches; operable with single effort without grasping.

nodes.label: 1132A.10 Door Signal Devices
nodes.rationale: Every primary entrance to a covered multifamily dwelling unit shall have a doorbell, buzzer, chime or equivalent; max 48 inches above floor; permanently wired.

nodes.label: 1133A Kitchens
nodes.rationale: Kitchens on accessible route; clear floor spaces at range, sink, appliances; U-shaped kitchens 60-inch clearance with parallel approach or 48-inch with forward approach.

nodes.label: 1133A.3 Removable Base Cabinets
nodes.rationale: Base cabinets under sinks and work surfaces shall be removable without specialized tools to provide knee and toe space.

nodes.label: 1133A.4 Countertops
nodes.rationale: Min 30 linear inches of countertop for sink; min 30 linear inches of work surface. Repositionable countertops required in at least 5% of covered dwelling units.

nodes.label: 1134A Bathing and Toilet Facilities (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: Two compliance options: Option 1 (all bathrooms comply) or Option 2 (one bathroom complies with full requirements; others comply with items 8-12).

nodes.label: 1134A.5 Bathtubs (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: 48x30 in clear floor space; reinforced walls for grab bars 32-38 in AFF; bathtub controls operable one-hand max 5 lb.

nodes.label: 1134A.6 Showers (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: Three acceptable shower stall configurations: 42x48 in with 36 in opening; 30x60 in with 60 in opening; 36x60 in with 36 in opening. Reinforced walls 32-38 in AFF for grab bars.

nodes.label: 1134A.7 Water Closets (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: Min 48-inch wide clear floor space; water closet centerline 17-18 in from wall/grab bar; min 15-in seat height; reinforced walls for grab bars.

nodes.label: 1134A.8 Lavatories, Vanities, Mirrors and Towel Fixtures (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: Centerline min 18 in from wall for forward approach (24 in for parallel); max 34 in rim height; removable or open knee space; mirrors and towels max 40 in AFF.
nodes.norm_label: 1134a.8 lavatories, vanities, mirrors and towel fixtures (dwelling units)

nodes.label: 1135A Laundry Rooms (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: If washers/dryers provided in dwelling units, one of each type shall be provided; front-loading preferred; management must provide assistive devices on request for top-loading machines.

nodes.label: 1136A Electrical Receptacle, Switch and Control Heights (Dwelling Units)
nodes.rationale: Receptacles: 15-48 inches AFF; switches/controls: 15-48 inches AFF; applies to 30-amp or less branch circuits.
nodes.norm_label: 1136a electrical receptacle, switch and control heights (dwelling units)

nodes.label: 1137A Other Features and Facilities
nodes.rationale: Division V provisions apply to features and facilities in common use areas on accessible floors or sites; not applicable to dwelling units unless otherwise specified.

nodes.label: 1138A.1 Space Allowances
nodes.rationale: Single wheelchair passage min 36 in; two wheelchair passing min 60 in; turning space 60-in diameter circle or T-shaped; clear floor space 30x48 in.

nodes.label: 1138A.3 Reach Ranges
nodes.rationale: Forward reach: max 48 in, min 15 in; side reach: max 48 in, min 15 in; obstructed reach limits vary with reach depth.

nodes.label: 1139A Accessible Drinking Fountains
nodes.rationale: Side approach not acceptable; spout max 36 in AFF; knee and toe space required; located in alcoves; 30x48 in clear floor space.

nodes.label: 1140A Accessible Telephones
nodes.rationale: At least one phone per floor shall be accessible; clear floor space 30x48 in; TTY required when 4+ pay phones on site and at least one is interior.

nodes.label: 1141A Accessible Swimming Pools
nodes.rationale: Pool deck areas must be accessible; pool entry/exit mechanism required; swimming pool lift device criteria specified.

nodes.label: 1142A Electrical Receptacle, Switch and Control Heights (Common Use)
nodes.rationale: Same height requirements as 1136A applied to common use areas: 15-48 inches AFF.
nodes.norm_label: 1142a electrical receptacle, switch and control heights (common use)

nodes.label: 1143A Signage
nodes.rationale: Signs not required within dwelling units. Identification signs comply with raised characters, Braille, and visual character height per Table 1143A.5.

nodes.label: 1150A Site Impracticality Tests
nodes.rationale: Three tests determine when accessible routes are impractical due to terrain: Test 1 (Individual Building - slopes >15%), Test 2 (Site Analysis - percentage of buildable area with <10% slope), Test 3 (Unusual Characteristics - floodplains, coastal high-hazard areas).

nodes.label: 1150A.2 Additional Requirements for Site Impracticality
nodes.rationale: Ground floor units not on accessible route still must comply with: grab bar reinforcement, 32-in door widths, lever hardware, door signal devices, 15-in water closet seat height, receptacle/switch heights, faucet controls.

nodes.label: Table 1124A.3.2 Elevator Car Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Specifies minimum elevator car interior dimensions by door location: centered (42x80x51x54 in), side/off-centered (36x68x51x54 in), any location (36x54x80x80 in or 36x60x60x60 in).

nodes.label: Table 1143A.5 Visual Character Height
nodes.rationale: Three tiers based on height above floor (40-70 in, 70-120 in, >120 in) and horizontal viewing distance; minimum character heights range from 5/8 inch to 3 inches.

nodes.label: Table 1143A.7.1 Braille Dimensions
nodes.rationale: Dot base diameter 0.059-0.063 in; dot height 0.025-0.037 in; inter-dot and inter-cell distances specified.

nodes.label: Section 1.1 General
nodes.rationale: Establishes the California Building Code as Part 2 of Title 24, California Code of Regulations, incorporating by adoption the 2021 International Building Code with California amendments.

nodes.label: 1.1.2 Purpose

nodes.label: 1.1.3 Scope

nodes.label: 1601.1 Scope
nodes.rationale: Establishes that Chapter 16 governs structural design of buildings, structures and portions thereof regulated by the CBC.

nodes.label: 1602.1 Notations
nodes.rationale: Defines load notation symbols (D, E, F, H, L, R, S, T, W, etc.) used throughout Chapter 16.

nodes.label: 1603.1 General (Construction Documents)
nodes.rationale: Requires construction documents to show structural member sizes, locations, and design loads per Sections 1603.1.1 through 1603.1.9.

nodes.label: 1604.1 General Design Requirements
nodes.rationale: Permits strength design, LRFD, ASD, empirical design or conventional construction as allowed by material chapters and referenced standards.

nodes.label: 1604.3 Serviceability
nodes.rationale: Requires structural systems to have adequate stiffness to limit deflections per Table 1604.3.

nodes.label: 1604.4 Analysis
nodes.rationale: Requires structural analysis to account for equilibrium, stability, geometric compatibility, and material properties; system must provide complete load path.

nodes.label: 1604.5 Risk Category
nodes.rationale: Requires each building to be assigned a risk category per Table 1604.5; used to determine design loads including wind and seismic.

nodes.label: 1604.9 Wind and Seismic Detailing
nodes.rationale: Lateral force-resisting systems must meet seismic detailing per ASCE 7 Chapters 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18 even when wind governs.

nodes.label: 1605.1 Load Combinations General
nodes.rationale: Buildings shall resist strength load combinations per ASCE 7 Section 2.3, ASD per ASCE 7 Section 2.4, or alternative ASD per Section 1605.2.

nodes.label: 1605.1.1 Stability
nodes.rationale: Overall structure stability (overturning, sliding, buoyancy) may use ASCE 7 Section 2.3 or 2.4 or Section 1605.2 load combinations.

nodes.label: 1605.2 Alternative ASD Load Combinations
nodes.rationale: Provides Equations 16-1 through 16-6 as alternative to ASCE 7 Section 2.4 ASD load combinations.

nodes.label: 1606.1 Dead Loads General
nodes.rationale: Dead loads are permanent loads as defined in Chapter 2.

nodes.label: 1607.3 Uniform Live Loads
nodes.rationale: Live loads shall be maximum expected for occupancy but not less than Table 1607.1 minimums.

nodes.label: 1607.12 Reduction in Uniform Live Loads
nodes.rationale: Minimum distributed live loads may be reduced per Equations 16-7 through 16-9 where tributary area x KLL >= 400 sq ft.

nodes.label: 1607.14.4 Photovoltaic Panel Systems
nodes.rationale: Roof structures supporting PV panel systems must be designed per Sections 1607.14.4.1 through 1607.14.4.5.

nodes.label: 1608.1 Snow Loads General
nodes.rationale: Design snow loads per ASCE 7 Chapter 7; roof load not less than Section 1607 requirements.

nodes.label: 1608.2 Ground Snow Loads
nodes.rationale: Ground snow loads from ASCE 7 or Figures 1608.2(1)/(2) for contiguous US; Table 1608.2 for Alaska.

nodes.label: 1609.1 Wind Loads Applications
nodes.rationale: Minimum wind loads per ASCE 7 Chapters 26-30; no reduction for shielding. Alternatives include ICC 600, AWC WFCM, AISI S230, TIA-222, ASCE 49.

nodes.label: 1609.2 Protection of Openings
nodes.rationale: Windborne debris regions: glazing must be impact-resistant or protected per ASTM E1996.

nodes.label: 1609.3 Basic Design Wind Speed
nodes.rationale: Basic design wind speed V determined from Figures 1609.3(1)-(12) by risk category.

nodes.label: 1609.3.1 Wind Speed Conversion
nodes.rationale: Converts basic wind speed V to ASD wind speed Vasd using Table 1609.3.1 or Equation 16-17 (Vasd = V * sqrt(0.6)).

nodes.label: 1609.4 Exposure Category
nodes.rationale: Exposure categories B, C, D defined by ground surface roughness in upwind direction.

nodes.label: 1610.1 Lateral Soil Pressures
nodes.rationale: Foundation and retaining walls must resist lateral soil loads per Table 1610.1; geotechnical investigation may override.

nodes.label: 1611.1 Design Rain Loads
nodes.rationale: Rain load per ASCE 7 Chapter 8; design rainfall based on 100-year 15-minute event. Equation 16-19: R = 5.2(ds + dh).

nodes.label: 1612.1 Flood Loads General
nodes.rationale: Within flood hazard areas, all new construction must resist flood hazards per ASCE 7 Chapter 5 and ASCE 24.

nodes.label: 1612.3 Establishment of Flood Hazard Areas
nodes.rationale: Requires adopting FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) and supporting data.

nodes.label: 1613.1 Earthquake Loads Scope
nodes.rationale: Every structure including nonstructural components must be designed for earthquake forces per ASCE 7 Chapters 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18.

nodes.label: 1613.2.1 Mapped Acceleration Parameters
nodes.rationale: Ss and S1 from Figures 1613.2.1(1)-(10) (MCEr ground motion maps).

nodes.label: 1613.2.2 Site Class Definitions
nodes.rationale: Site classified A-F per ASCE 7 Chapter 20; default Site Class D if soil properties unknown.

nodes.label: 1613.2.3 Site Coefficients and MCE Spectral Accelerations
nodes.rationale: SMS = Fa*Ss (Eq 16-20); SM1 = Fv*S1 (Eq 16-21); Fa and Fv from Tables 1613.2.3(1) and 1613.2.3(2).
nodes.norm_label: 1613.2.3 site coefficients and mce spectral accelerations

nodes.label: 1613.2.4 Design Spectral Response Acceleration Parameters
nodes.rationale: SDS = (2/3)SMS (Eq 16-22); SD1 = (2/3)SM1 (Eq 16-23); 5% damped design spectral response accelerations.

nodes.label: 1613.2.5 Determination of Seismic Design Category
nodes.rationale: SDC A-F from Tables 1613.2.5(1) and (2) based on SDS, SD1, and risk category. OSHPD structures default to SDC D minimum.

nodes.label: 1614.1 Atmospheric Ice Loads
nodes.rationale: Ice-sensitive structures designed per ASCE 7 Chapter 10.

nodes.label: Dead Load
nodes.rationale: Permanent load from weight of construction materials, fixed service equipment, and similar; defined as D in Section 1602.1.

nodes.label: Live Load
nodes.rationale: Load produced by use and occupancy; defined as L in Section 1602.1.

nodes.label: Snow Load
nodes.rationale: Load from accumulation of snow on roofs; defined as S in Section 1602.1.

nodes.label: Wind Load
nodes.rationale: Load due to wind pressure; defined as W in Section 1602.1.

nodes.label: Earthquake Load
nodes.rationale: Combined horizontal and vertical earthquake-induced forces; defined as E per ASCE 7 Section 12.4.

nodes.label: Rain Load
nodes.rationale: Load from accumulation of rainwater on roofs; defined as R in Section 1602.1.

nodes.label: Flood Load
nodes.rationale: Flood load per ASCE 7 Chapter 5; defined as Fa in Section 1602.1.

nodes.label: Risk Category
nodes.rationale: Classification I-IV indicating hazard to human life; governs design loads for wind, seismic, snow, and other hazards.

nodes.label: Seismic Design Category (SDC)
nodes.rationale: Category A-F assigned based on SDS, SD1, and risk category; governs permissible structural systems and detailing requirements.

nodes.label: Site Class
nodes.rationale: Classification A-F based on soil properties; used to determine site coefficients Fa and Fv for seismic design.

nodes.label: Design Spectral Response Acceleration (SDS, SD1)
nodes.rationale: 5%-damped design spectral accelerations at short period (SDS) and 1-second period (SD1); two-thirds of MCE spectral accelerations.

nodes.label: Basic Design Wind Speed (V)
nodes.rationale: 3-second gust wind speed at 33 ft above ground for Exposure C; varies by risk category.

nodes.label: Flood Hazard Area
nodes.rationale: Areas identified on FEMA FIRM; new construction must resist flood effects.

nodes.label: Load Combinations
nodes.rationale: Combinations of loads (D, L, S, W, E, R, etc.) used to establish design forces; strength design via ASCE 7 Section 2.3, ASD via ASCE 7 Section 2.4 or alternative Section 1605.2.

nodes.label: Seismic Force-Resisting System
nodes.rationale: Structural system designed and detailed to resist earthquake forces; must comply with ASCE 7 Chapter 12 limitations and Table 12.2-1.

nodes.label: Ponding
nodes.rationale: Progressive deflection and accumulation of water on roofs; evaluated per ASCE 7 Chapters 7 and 8.

nodes.label: Structural Integrity
nodes.rationale: High-rise Risk Category III/IV buildings must have continuous load paths (ties) to prevent progressive collapse.

nodes.label: Live Load Reduction
nodes.rationale: Permitted reduction to minimum distributed live loads where KLL*AT >= 400 sq ft using Equation 16-7; limits apply by element type.

nodes.label: 1801A General
nodes.rationale: Scope section for Chapter 18A; applies to DSA-SS, DSA-SS/CC, and OSHPD applications including public schools, community colleges, hospitals, and correctional treatment centers.

nodes.label: 1801A.1.1 Application
nodes.rationale: Specifies that Chapter 18A applies to DSA-SS (1.9.2.1, 1.9.2.2) and OSHPD (1.10.1, 1.10.4) regulated structures.

nodes.label: 1802A Design Basis
nodes.rationale: Requires use of allowable stress design load combinations from ASCE 7 Section 2.4 or Section 1605.2 alternative.

nodes.label: 1803A Geotechnical Investigations
nodes.rationale: Master section governing all geotechnical investigation requirements for DSA and OSHPD regulated structures.

nodes.label: 1803A.1 General
nodes.rationale: Requires investigations under responsible charge of a California registered geotechnical engineer; reports subject to enforcement agency approval.

nodes.label: 1803A.2 Investigations Required
nodes.rationale: General trigger for geotechnical investigations; exceptions for small wood-frame buildings outside fault/seismic hazard zones.

nodes.label: 1803A.3 Basis of Investigation
nodes.rationale: Soil classification based on borings/test pits; additional studies for slope stability, liquefaction, expansiveness.

nodes.label: 1803A.3.1 Scope of Investigation
nodes.rationale: Minimum one boring per 5,000 sq ft with minimum two per building; borings must be of sufficient depth and size.

nodes.label: 1803A.4 Qualified Representative
nodes.rationale: Requires a fully qualified representative on site during all boring or sampling operations.

nodes.label: 1803A.5 Investigated Conditions
nodes.rationale: Umbrella section covering 12 specific investigation conditions from soil classification to seismic categories.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.1 Classification
nodes.rationale: Requires soil classification per ASTM D2487.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.2 Questionable Soil
nodes.rationale: Building official may require geotechnical investigation where soil classification or strength is in doubt.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.3 Expansive Soil
nodes.rationale: Defines expansive soil by four criteria: PI>=15 (ASTM D4318), >10% passing No.200 sieve (ASTM D422), >10% <5 micrometers (ASTM D422), or expansion index >20 (ASTM D4829).

nodes.label: 1803A.5.4 Ground-Water Table
nodes.rationale: Investigation required when floor below grade; determines if groundwater within 5 ft of lowest floor.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.5 Deep Foundations
nodes.rationale: Nine mandatory investigation items for deep foundations including type recommendations, driving criteria, load test requirements.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.6 Rock Strata
nodes.rationale: Borings required to assess rock competency and load-bearing capacity where rock structure varies.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.7 Excavation Near Foundations
nodes.rationale: Requires registered design professional assessment and site-specific plans before excavation reducing foundation support.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.8 Compacted Fill Material
nodes.rationale: Seven-item investigation checklist for shallow foundations on compacted fill >12 inches deep.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.9 Controlled Low-Strength Material (CLSM)
nodes.rationale: Five-item investigation checklist when shallow foundations bear on CLSM.

nodes.label: 1803A.5.10 Alternate Setback and Clearance
nodes.rationale: Investigation may be required by building official for alternate slope setbacks; must consider slope material, height, gradient, load intensity.

nodes.label: 1803A.7 Geotechnical Reporting
nodes.rationale: 12-item minimum content list for geotechnical report including boring logs, soil profile, water table, foundation recommendations.

nodes.label: 1803A.8 Geotechnical Peer Review
nodes.rationale: [DSA-SS and DSA-SS/CC] Peer review by California-licensed geotechnical engineer may be required for alternate foundation designs, ground improvements, or slope stabilization.

hyperedges.label: Accessible Route Provisions Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 11B-206 (scoping) and 11B-402 through 11B-407 (Division 4 technical) together constitute the complete accessible route requirement framework: where required, what components are allowed, and how each component must be built.

hyperedges.label: Alteration Path of Travel Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 11B-202 and 11B-202.4 together with the valuation threshold and unreasonable hardship concepts govern the entire path-of-travel upgrade regime for alterations, forming a unified compliance framework with cost balancing provisions.

hyperedges.label: Residential Dwelling Unit Accessibility Framework
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 11B-233 (public housing scoping) and 11B-809 (technical requirements) combined with mobility and adaptable feature concepts form the complete residential dwelling unit accessibility framework applied across all public housing construction.

hyperedges.label: Emergency Sleeping Cabin Life Safety Requirements
hyperedges.rationale: Sections P104.4 (egress), P104.8 (smoke alarms), and P104.9 (CO alarms) collectively form the life-safety egress and alarm requirement set for emergency sleeping cabins.

hyperedges.label: Loft Access and Egress Options
hyperedges.rationale: Sections P108.2.1 through P108.2.4 collectively define the permissible loft access and safety guard options for emergency housing lofts.

hyperedges.label: Dependent Unit Sanitation Facility Requirements
hyperedges.rationale: Sections P110.2, P110.3, and P110.4 together form the sanitation and waste management requirements for dependent unit occupants in emergency housing sites.

hyperedges.label: Seismic Analysis Suite: Loading + Structural Performance + Component Design
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 3103F.4, 3104F, and 3107F together define the complete seismic analysis workflow: earthquake loads/parameters → two-level performance criteria and analytical procedures → material strain limits and component capacity for MOT structures.

hyperedges.label: Audit-Rating-Action Triad: Inspection Scope + Assessment Ratings + Follow-up Actions
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 3102F.3 (audit scope), Table 31F-2-4 (assessment ratings OSAR/SSAR/ICAR), and Table 31F-2-5 (RAP remedial priorities) form an integrated compliance framework for evaluating and acting on MOT condition.

hyperedges.label: Mooring System: Environmental Loads + Mooring Analysis + Hardware Design
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 3103F.5 (environmental forces on vessels), 3105F.2 (mooring analysis procedures), and 3105F.8 (mooring hardware sizing and safety factors) together constitute the complete mooring system design requirement chain.

hyperedges.label: Lateral Force-Resisting System Design Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 2305, 2306.2, and 2306.3 together govern the complete design of wood-frame lateral force-resisting systems: 2305 establishes the general design requirements and references AWC SDPWS, 2306.2 provides diaphragm-specific allowable shear values, and 2306.3 provides shear wall allowable shear values — all must be satisfied together for a code-compliant LFRS.

hyperedges.label: Wood Truss Design, Submittal, and Quality Assurance Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 2303.4.1, 2303.4.1.2, and 2303.4.1.3 collectively establish the complete truss design requirements: design drawing content (2303.4.1), permanent restraint methods (2303.4.1.2), and registered design professional requirements for long-span trusses ≥60 ft (2303.4.1.3).

hyperedges.label: Wood Decay and Termite Protection Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Section 2304.12 (protection requirements by location), 2303.1.9 (preservative-treated wood standards and labeling), and AWPA U1 collectively form the complete wood protection system — identifying where, what treatment standard applies, and how treated material must be identified.

hyperedges.label: High-Rise Building Life Safety System Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 403.3, 403.4.7, 403.4.8, 403.5.4, and 403.6.1 together constitute the integrated life safety system requirements—sprinklers, smoke control, emergency power, smokeproof enclosures, and fire service elevators—that collectively define high-rise fire protection strategy

hyperedges.label: Group I-2 Smoke Compartmentation and Egress Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 407.5, 407.5.1, 407.6, and 407.7 together define the defend-in-place strategy for I-2 occupancies: smoke barriers subdivide floors into compartments, automatic-closing doors restrict smoke movement, and sprinklers protect throughout—all required simultaneously

hyperedges.label: Group H-5 Fabrication Area Safety Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 415.11.1, 415.11.1.1, 415.11.2, and 415.11.3 together form the H-5 semiconductor fabrication safety framework: quantity limits per fabrication area, HPM restrictions in corridors, and separate service corridors for HPM transport

hyperedges.label: Occupant Load to Egress Sizing Pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: These three sections form an integrated requirement: occupant load is calculated per Table 1004.5, that load drives required egress capacity per Section 1005.3 (width = OL x capacity factor), and the occupant load also determines the number of exits required per Section 1006.2.1 and Table 1006.2.1.

hyperedges.label: Three-Part Means of Egress System
hyperedges.rationale: Exit access (Sections 1016-1021), exit (Sections 1022-1027), and exit discharge (Sections 1028-1029) together constitute the complete means of egress pathway required by Section 1001.1; each part has its own dimensional, fire-resistance, and signage requirements.

hyperedges.label: Accessible Means of Egress and Refuge System
hyperedges.rationale: These sections collectively govern accessible means of egress: Section 1009.1 requires accessible means of egress from each accessible space, Section 1009.3 specifies accessible stairway requirements (48-inch clear width), and Section 1009.6 establishes area of refuge requirements (size, separation, two-way communication) as the shelter-in-place component of the accessible egress strategy.

hyperedges.label: Occupancy-Based Sprinkler Trigger Thresholds
hyperedges.rationale: These sections collectively define fire area thresholds (5,000–24,000 sq ft) and occupant load thresholds (100–300) that trigger sprinkler requirements for various occupancy groups, forming a coherent threshold-based requirement system.

hyperedges.label: High-Rise Building Integrated Fire Protection Requirements
hyperedges.rationale: For high-rise buildings (occupied floors >75 ft above lowest fire department vehicle access), these sections together mandate automatic smoke detection, emergency voice/alarm communication system, fire command center, zoning annunciator panel, and firefighter smoke control panel—a unified heightened protection system.

hyperedges.label: Smoke Control Method Alternatives
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 909.6, 909.7, and 909.8 define the three permitted mechanical smoke control design methods—pressurization, airflow, and exhaust—which collectively constitute the complete set of code-recognized approaches for mechanical smoke control.

hyperedges.label: Accessible Parking System (Percentage, Location, Design)
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1109A.3 (required quantity), 1109A.7 (location criteria), and 1109A.8 (design/construction standards) together form the complete accessible parking requirement framework for covered multifamily dwellings.

hyperedges.label: Primary Entry Door Accessibility System

hyperedges.label: Building Permit Process: Application → Plan Review → Permit Issuance → Inspections → Certificate of Occupancy

hyperedges.label: Deep Foundation Design-Detailing-Installation Requirement Set

hyperedges.label: Geotechnical Investigation — Report — Peer Review Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1803A.5 (investigation conditions), 1803A.7 (reporting requirements), and 1803A.8 (peer review) together form a complete investigation-to-approval workflow for DSA-SS/CC projects.

hyperedges.label: Seismic Deep Foundation Design Set — SDC D-F
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1810A.2.4.1 (curvature demands), 1810A.3.6.1 (seismic splice requirements), and 1810A.3.9.4 (seismic reinforcement) together form the SDC D-F seismic detailing requirement set for deep foundations.

hyperedges.label: Expansive Soil Identification and Foundation Design Set
hyperedges.rationale: Section 1803A.5.3 (identification criteria using ASTM tests), 1808A.6.1 (structural foundation design), and 1808A.6.2 (slab-on-ground design) together form the complete expansive soil mitigation chain from identification through design.

hyperedges.label: Structural Steel Seismic Inspection Requirement Set
hyperedges.rationale: Sections 1705A.2.1 (quality assurance), 1705A.13.1 (seismic special inspections for SDC D-F), and 1705A.14 (nondestructive testing) together form the complete structural steel seismic inspection requirement set, all invoking AISC 341 Chapter J/N with California modifications.

hyperedges.rationale: Section 1705A.15 together with ASTM E605 (thickness and density) and ASTM E736 (bond strength) form an inseparable inspection triad; all three must be satisfied to comply with SFRM special inspection requirements for floor, roof, wall and structural member applications.
